title: Ripple CEO Says XRP and RLUSD Work Together to Meet Customer Needs
summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said Ripple USD (RLUSD) competes with other stablecoins while complementing XRP. His comments connected the assets through customer needs and his preference for bringing more financial activity onto the XRP Ledger. Garlinghouse Places RLUSD Alongside XRP Ripple CEO Brad ...
content:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said Ripple USD (RLUSD) competes with other stablecoins while complementing XRP. His comments connected the assets through customer needs and his preference for bringing more financial activity onto the XRP Ledger.

Key Takeaways

  • Garlinghouse said RLUSD competes with other stablecoins, not XRP.
  • XRP Ledger accounts require XRP reserves, while RLUSD requires a trust line.
  • Ripple prioritizes XRP where it suits customers, using fiat or RLUSD otherwise.

Garlinghouse Places RLUSD Alongside XRP

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse stated on X on Nov. 3 that RLUSD and XRP served complementary purposes, identifying other stablecoins as RLUSD’s competitors. He addressed the relationship in separate replies to users on X, who discussed liquidity and the assets’ different functions.

Garlinghouse outlined where RLUSD competes:

“RLUSD isn’t competing with XRP. It’s competing with other stablecoins. Use case matters, and I want those use cases running on the XRPL.”

His statement was in response to a post arguing that deeper liquidity on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) could make XRP easier to use over time, while describing the price impact without direct use as indirect. That post raised a broader question about adoption: whether XRP would become a specialized institutional asset with restricted liquidity or achieve widespread use.

How XRP Supports RLUSD Activity on the Ledger

For businesses settling dollar-denominated obligations, RLUSD offers a payment asset designed to maintain a dollar value through its reserve backing and redemption structure. Ripple identifies payments, remittances, and treasury flows among its intended uses. That focus allows a company to move a dollar balance onchain while keeping the amount it owes and pays expressed in the same currency.

Every RLUSD transfer on XRPL falls under the network’s XRP transaction fee requirements, which consume a small quantity of XRP. That amount is destroyed, with the required fee varying by transaction type and network load. This network charge is separate from the value being transferred, so sending RLUSD does not require converting the payment amount into XRP.

Beyond fees, XRP can connect token markets when exchanging through it offers a better rate than a direct trade. Evernorth chief business officer Sagar Shah described this liquidity-routing role alongside RLUSD in May, positioning the stablecoin as the dollar-denominated asset. The ledger’s exchange mechanism can combine direct trades with routes through XRP to obtain a better overall rate.

Customer Needs Shape Ripple’s Asset Choices

In a separate reply to another user on X, Garlinghouse endorsed RLUSD and XRP’s distinct roles:

“Complementary, not competitive.”

The post he replied to explained that accounts require XRP reserves, while holders opt into RLUSD through a trust line, an account setting for accepting an issued token. XRP itself can be held without establishing a trust line.

At Swell, Ripple’s annual conference, Garlinghouse had described a customer-focused approach to XRP adoption in remarks shared Oct. 28. He said Ripple would prioritize XRP where it suited customer needs while using fiat currencies or RLUSD for other transactions. He preferred XRP handling a small share of a customer’s activity over none.

Among institutional providers supporting both assets, BNY confirmed Oct. 27 that eligible clients could safeguard, hold, and transfer XRP and RLUSD through its custody platform. The bank incorporated that access within its existing governance and operational controls. Its expanded custody offering built on BNY’s role as the primary custodian of RLUSD reserves.

title: US midterms election 2026 live: Democrats 6 seats short of Senate majority
summary: Follow live coverage of the 2026 US midterm elections, including key congressional races, crypto-backed candidates and what the results could mean for digital asset regulation.
content:
Within the next few hours, we will begin to learn whether President Donald Trump’s Republican Party has managed to retain control of the US Congress, determining his ability to advance his legislative agenda during the final two years of his term.

What the crypto industry needs to know:

  • All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 Senate seats are up for grabs. 
  • The results could influence the future of US cryptocurrency regulation, including the stalled CLARITY Act, and potentially intensify scrutiny of Trump’s crypto ventures if Democrats gain control of either chamber.
  • In the Senate, Democrats and allied independents have secured 45 seats to Republicans’ 36, including seats not up for election. Democrats have won 108 House seats to Republicans’ 63.
  • Democrats need 51 Senate seats and 218 House seats to secure majorities in both chambers.
  • The Blockchain Association’s election dashboard identifies 62 priority congressional races, including 18 Senate and 44 House contests.

Live election updates

Follow the latest developments in congressional races attracting crypto industry spending, election results and reactions from prediction markets. Cointelegraph is using live election results data from the Associated Press. Updates appear in reverse chronological order.

Nov. 3 at 10:02 ET:

Democrats six seats short of Senate majority

Democrats and allied independents stood at 45 Senate seats as of 10:02 pm ET, six short of the 51 needed for a majority.

Their path includes retaining Democratic-held seats in Oregon, Michigan and Minnesota and flipping three additional Republican-held seats. Democrats have already picked up North Carolina.

NBC News has projected that Democrat Annie Andrews will defeat incumbent Republican Senator Darline Graham in South Carolina in a major upset. Associated Press has not yet called this race.

Nov. 3 at 21:21 ET:

Crypto-backed Republican Andy Barr wins Kentucky Senate seat

Republican Representative Andy Barr has won Kentucky’s US Senate race, sending a supporter of the CLARITY and GENIUS Acts to the upper chamber.

Fairshake-affiliated political action committees spent more than $7 million supporting Barr in the Republican primary. Barr has also introduced legislation aimed at protecting lawful businesses, including crypto firms, from debanking.

Nov. 3 at 21:17 ET: 

Democrat Juliana Stratton wins Illinois Senate seat

Democrat Juliana Stratton has won Illinois’ US Senate race, succeeding retiring Democratic Sen. Dick Durbin.

Stratton advanced through the Democratic primary despite substantial opposition from crypto-backed PAC Fairshake, which had spent more than $5.5 million against her by early March.

Nov. 3 at 21:05 ET: 

Republican Hageman wins Wyoming Senate seat

Republican Representative Harriet Hageman has won Wyoming’s US Senate race against Democrat James Byrd, succeeding retiring crypto advocate Senator Cynthia Lummis.

Lummis, who chairs the Senate Banking Subcommittee on Digital Assets, sponsored the BITCOIN Act of 2025 to establish a US strategic Bitcoin reserve and has supported the CLARITY and GENIUS Acts.

Hageman has also backed cryptocurrency legislation, voting to pass the CLARITY and GENIUS Acts in 2025 and the FIT21 market structure bill in 2024. She also cosponsored legislation seeking to prohibit the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency, according to Stand With Crypto. The advocacy group lists no documented position on cryptocurrency for Byrd.

Nov. 3 at 21:05 ET:

Prediction markets price Democratic control of both chambers

Kalshi and Polymarket traders now give Democrats a 99% chance of winning Senate control and price House control at nearly 100%. It came as Democrats flipped North Carolina’s Senate seat, while holding Georgia and New Hampshire.

Nov. 3 at 20:08 ET:

Democratic Senate odds climb above 90%

Prediction markets increasingly favored Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress on Tuesday evening.

As of 8:05 pm ET, the Blockchain Association’s election dashboard showed Democratic Senate-control odds at 94% on Kalshi and 93% on Polymarket, up from 75% and 75.5%, respectively, earlier in the day. Democratic House-control odds stood at 98% and 99%.

It comes as Democrats and allied independents have secured 42 Senate seats to Republicans’ 31.

Nov. 3 at 20:01 ET:

Democratic senators Markey and Coons win reelection

Massachusetts Senator Ed Markey and Delaware Senator Chris Coons, both Democrats, win reelection, according to the Associated Press.

Markey voted against the GENIUS stablecoin bill in 2025, while Coons has criticized President Donald Trump’s crypto ventures, calling his latest memecoin-holder event “corruption.”

Nov. 3 at 19:57 ET:

Democrat Jon Ossoff retains Georgia Senate seat

Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff has won reelection in Georgia, beating Republican Representative Mike Collins.

Ossoff expressed support for impeaching Trump in April 2025 over plans to host a private dinner for top holders of the president’s TRUMP memecoin, arguing that the arrangement amounted to selling access to the presidency.

Nov. 3 at 19:41 ET:

1inch sees agencies driving US crypto regulation

Maylea Ma, deputy general counsel at 1inch, said she expects federal agencies to drive the next phase of crypto regulation.

The election could reshape the path forward for the stalled CLARITY Act, but Ma said “real movement” in US digital-asset regulation over the next few years will come from the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Treasury, rather than Congress.

Ma said those agencies were increasingly engaging with crypto projects. However, agency engagement does not provide the stability the industry had hoped to secure through legislation.

“The long-term goal, of course, remains a statute that cannot be reversed every time a government changes,” said Ma.

Nov. 3 at 19:09 ET:

CLARITY opponent Wasserman Schultz wins reelection

Democratic Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz wins Florida’s 20th Congressional District. Wasserman Schultz voted against the CLARITY crypto market structure bill when it passed the House in July 2025.

Nov. 3 at 19:05 ET:

Democrat Warner retains Virginia Senate seat 

Democratic Senator Mark Warner has won re-election in Virginia, defeating Republican challenger Bert Mizusawa. Warner was widely favored to win.

Warner voted against advancing the CLARITY Act in September, arguing that crypto legislation needs safeguards against President Donald Trump personally benefiting from the industry. Warner supports establishing federal rules for digital assets, with his opposition to the bill focused on its ethics protections.

Nov. 3 at 18:00 ET:

First US polls close

The first polls in the US midterm elections closed at 6 pm ET in parts of Indiana and Kentucky. The remaining polls in both states close at 7 pm ET.

Polls also close at 7 pm ET in Georgia and Virginia, followed by Ohio at 7:30 pm ET, where Republican Sen. Jon Husted faces Democrat Sherrod Brown in a race drawing major crypto industry spending.

Nov. 3 at 11:37 ET:

Early voting surpasses 57 million ahead of midterms

More than 57 million Americans had cast ballots as of Monday, with early voting surpassing 2022 levels in several closely watched states, according to the Associated Press.

Current balance of power in the US House and Senate. Source: Blockchain Association

Other key crypto races to watch

Ohio Senate: Jon Husted vs Sherrod Brown

In Ohio, Republican Sen. Jon Husted faces Democrat Sherrod Brown, a longtime crypto critic, in a race that has attracted approximately $63 million in crypto industry spending. That includes about $56 million from Fairshake and $7 million from the Winklevoss-backed Digital Freedom Fund, with both groups spending to support Husted or oppose Brown.

Crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto characterizes Brown as strongly opposed to cryptocurrency, citing 17 statements and his 2024 vote against overturning the SEC’s SAB 121 crypto custody accounting guidance.

Brown was also targeted by crypto industry spending in 2024, when Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs spent more than $40 million supporting Republican Bernie Moreno, who defeated Brown in that year’s Senate election.

Nebraska Senate: Pete Ricketts vs Dan Osborn

Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts faces independent challenger Dan Osborn in Nebraska, where crypto political action committee Fairshake had spent nearly $11 million supporting Ricketts, according to an Oct. 27 report by the Washington Examiner.

More recent spending data shows Fairshake-affiliated crypto super PAC Defend American Jobs spent approximately $13.5 million opposing Osborn, according to Federal Election Commission data compiled by Bankrolled as of Nov. 3.

Ricketts, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, has supported cryptocurrency legislation including the CLARITY Act and GENIUS Act. He voted to advance the CLARITY Act out of committee in May and supported an unsuccessful Senate procedural vote on the legislation in September, according to crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto.

Texas Senate: Ken Paxton vs James Talarico

In Texas, Republican Ken Paxton faces Democrat James Talarico, with the Winklevoss-backed Digital Freedom Fund supporting Paxton, despite both candidates receiving A ratings from crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto.

Paxton has called for the passage of the CLARITY Act, arguing that clear regulations are necessary to maintain US competitiveness in digital assets. In a June statement, he said the country must become the “crypto capital of the world” and support innovation and growth.

Talarico has similarly called for clear regulations that protect consumers while allowing innovation. As a Texas state representative, he also voted in 2025 to establish a state strategic Bitcoin reserve, according to legislative records cited by Stand With Crypto.

Maine Senate: Troy Jackson vs Susan Collins

Maine senator Susan Collins was one of four Republicans to oppose advancing the CLARITY Act in September, expressing concerns over its impact on bank deposits. She now faces Democrat Troy Jackson to defend her seat. 

Unlike Collins, Jackson has expressed support for clear cryptocurrency legislation in the run-up to the election. According to Stand with Crypto, which rates Jackson as “very pro crypto”, he called to end the debanking of “lawful crypto businesses, and ensure Americans’ right to self-custody digital assets.”

Crypto super PACs spend millions to influence Congress

Fairshake, backed by Coinbase, Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz, has led the spending through its affiliated super PACs, Defend American Jobs and Protect Progress. In early October, the group announced support for 32 incumbent House candidates, including 19 Republicans and 13 Democrats, all of whom voted in favor of the CLARITY Act in 2025.

Other crypto-aligned groups include the Digital Freedom Fund, backed by Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, the twin co-founders of crypto exchange Gemini, and Fellowship PAC, which has supported candidates from both parties.

title: Coinbase Explains Multi-User Architecture as Crypto Accounts Become More Complex
summary: Coinbase published an engineering account of its move toward multi-user infrastructure on October 29, describing how one account or organisation can…
content:
TL;DR: Coinbase published an engineering account of its move toward multi-user infrastructure on October 29, describing how one account or organisation can involve several people with different privileges. A blog describing architecture cannot prove that every application and endpoint is free of bugs.

Account controls rarely make headlines until something fails. But the ability to limit who can initiate and approve a transaction is one of the main differences between a personal wallet and an institution-ready service. Coinbase’s design discussion is a reminder that software architecture can shape real financial risk.

What the primary source establishes

Coinbase published an engineering account of its move toward multi-user infrastructure on October 29, describing how one account or organisation can involve several people with different privileges. The company discussed a distinction between the person acting and the entity on whose behalf an action occurs. This is a technical design explanation, not a claim that all customer products immediately acquired the same administrative features. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

When a platform starts with one person per account, permissions can be straightforward. Business accounts, joint processes and delegated roles complicate the model. Systems must establish who is authenticated, which resources they can access and what actions the organisation has allowed. Failing to make those checks consistent can create privacy and security problems even if the underlying authentication process works.

Why this matters beyond the headline

This matters because crypto businesses increasingly resemble financial organisations with staff, service providers and internal controls. A trading desk may want one employee to prepare an operation and another to approve it. Clear identity and authorisation boundaries are essential to making those workflows auditable. They are also an everyday security feature, not merely an enterprise convenience.

A crypto incident produces several separate timelines: containment, investigation, recovery and a return to reliable service. Those phases can overlap without finishing together. A traced wallet is not automatically frozen; a frozen balance is not automatically returned; and a reopened withdrawal route is not a completed security audit. Keeping those differences visible helps readers judge progress more accurately.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: Binance’s earlier staged withdrawal restart and Bitcoin payment infrastructure and node software context. They explain related market structure and should not be mistaken for evidence that every new proposal is already live.

What the announcement does not prove

A blog describing architecture cannot prove that every application and endpoint is free of bugs. Permission checks can be correct in one service and inconsistent elsewhere, especially during migration. Nor does a multi-user model replace strong authentication, careful device management or transaction-specific controls on sensitive funds movement.

Operational controls matter most when a business is under stress. Security announcements should identify the system affected, the customers who can act, the evidence supporting any recovery number and what remains uncertain. Clear scope protects users from false reassurance and from unnecessary panic. It also provides a sensible basis for follow-up accountability.

What to watch next

The next valuable evidence will be product-level rollout details, documented access roles and whether enterprise customers can adopt least-privilege policies without workarounds. The broader lesson is that the security of a digital-asset account often depends as much on internal identity systems as on the cryptography protecting a blockchain transaction.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: XRP Millionaire Wallets Hit 2026 High Despite Price Weakness
summary: XRP wallets holding at least 1 million tokens reached their highest count of 2026, according to Santiment. The analytics firm interpreted the increase during price weakness as a sign of accumulation, with stronger confirmation dependent on a sustained recovery. XRP Million-Token Wallet Count Reaches...
content:
XRP wallets holding at least 1 million tokens reached their highest count of 2026, according to Santiment. The analytics firm interpreted the increase during price weakness as a sign of accumulation, with stronger confirmation dependent on a sustained recovery.

Key Takeaways

  • Santiment counted 2,147 wallets holding at least 1 million XRP.
  • The group expanded by 28 addresses in 10 days, including 18 in three days.
  • Santiment tied a constructive setup to XRP holding $1.20 to $1.25 with the count above 2,140.

XRP Million-Token Wallet Count Reaches Yearly High

Blockchain analytics firm Santiment highlighted expanding large-holder participation on X on Nov. 3. Its XRP whale wallet growth figures tracked addresses meeting a minimum balance threshold during price weakness. Santiment stated:

“XRP now has 2,147 wallets holding at least 1M tokens, the highest count of 2026.”

The group gained 28 wallets over the preceding 10 days, including 18 during the final three days. Those shorter-period additions accounted for nearly two-thirds of the overall increase. Santiment said large holders tended to have longer time horizons than short-term traders, interpreting the expansion as evidence that substantial balances were being built.

A similar divergence appeared in August, when million-token XRP wallets increased by 32 over three months while the token’s market capitalization declined 29%. The latest figures cover a shorter period and show faster net address growth. The “millionaire” classification describes token holdings, with each qualifying address containing at least 1 million XRP.

Address Data Separates Holder Growth From Trading Activity

Santiment’s holder-distribution methodology measures distinct addresses grouped by token balances. An address crossing the 1 million XRP threshold increases the count, while one falling below it reduces the tally. The measure therefore tracks membership in a balance category; purchase volume requires separate evidence.

The relationship between addresses and investors also depends on how funds are held. XRP Ledger accounts can contain pooled exchange balances, with platforms typically holding customer XRP in a few shared accounts. Consequently, the number of qualifying addresses cannot establish how many individual investors hold that amount.

Separate measures capture other forms of activity. In September, Santiment recorded 1,917 large XRP transactions as the token crossed $1.60. That transaction tally measured transfers above a dollar threshold, whereas the latest finding tracks addresses meeting a minimum token balance.

Santiment Links Stronger Confirmation to Price Recovery

Broader network activity also increased, with 7,934 new XRP wallets created on Nov. 1, the sixth-highest daily total of 2026, Santiment reported. That measure captured newly created addresses across balance sizes. The two findings describe different aspects of participation: account creation and the distribution of large balances.

Following the Binance hack, the firm suggested that some users might have shifted toward self-custody of crypto assets. It presented that connection as a possible explanation for the earlier wallet-creation surge. Its latest large-holder assessment instead focused on whether the expanding group persisted through subsequent price moves.

Holding roughly $1.20 to $1.25 while the count remained above 2,140 would keep the longer-term setup constructive, the firm stated. Santiment added:

“A reclaim of psychological supports of $1.30, followed by $1.40, while large-wallet numbers keep rising would provide much stronger confirmation that accumulation is confirming every price rise.”

title: Hong Kong Launches Post-Quantum Preparation Toolkit for Banks
summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology announced a post-quantum cryptography assessment toolkit on November 2.
content:
TL;DR: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology announced a post-quantum cryptography assessment toolkit on November 2. Post-quantum migration is not the same thing as making every blockchain or bank system instantly quantum-secure.

Good security planning is often unglamorous. Discovering where keys are issued, which partners rely on them and when equipment will be replaced is difficult work, but it makes future transitions possible. The banking sector has a reason to start early because data captured today can remain sensitive long after the original connection has ended.

What the primary source establishes

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology announced a post-quantum cryptography assessment toolkit on November 2. The initiative is aimed at helping banks understand where current cryptographic systems might need upgrades as quantum capabilities develop. It is a preparation programme, not a declaration that quantum computers have broken banking or cryptocurrency encryption. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

Large organisations use cryptography in certificates, customer authentication, interbank links, software updates and the storage of sensitive data. Migrating those systems can take years because algorithms, devices, vendors and legacy applications must remain interoperable. A toolkit can help identify dependencies, prioritise sensitive data and test readiness for future standards before a forced emergency transition.

Why this matters beyond the headline

The HKMA has pointed to gaps in sector readiness and ambitions to improve preparedness by 2030. The most immediate benefit may be governance: teams can assign ownership of the inventory and agree which systems require the longest lead time. That is more useful than debating a speculative date on which a general-purpose quantum computer could break a particular cryptographic scheme.

A crypto incident produces several separate timelines: containment, investigation, recovery and a return to reliable service. Those phases can overlap without finishing together. A traced wallet is not automatically frozen; a frozen balance is not automatically returned; and a reopened withdrawal route is not a completed security audit. Keeping those differences visible helps readers judge progress more accurately.

For additional perspective, it is worth reading our existing reporting on Binance’s earlier staged withdrawal restart and Bitcoin payment infrastructure and node software context. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

What the announcement does not prove

Post-quantum migration is not the same thing as making every blockchain or bank system instantly quantum-secure. Different primitives face different levels of risk, and some proposed methods affect key size, verification performance or compatibility. The toolkit’s output is an assessment input, not a substitute for independent engineering and formal testing.

Operational controls matter most when a business is under stress. Security announcements should identify the system affected, the customers who can act, the evidence supporting any recovery number and what remains uncertain. Clear scope protects users from false reassurance and from unnecessary panic. It also provides a sensible basis for follow-up accountability.

What to watch next

Watch whether participating institutions publish migration road maps, begin procurement changes and test post-quantum authentication with core systems. For crypto readers, it is a reminder to separate near-term operational security from longer-term cryptographic research. No credible reading of the announcement implies that Bitcoin private keys are currently being routinely cracked by quantum machines.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Mercado Bitcoin Vows to Cover Customer Losses After Massive Hack
summary: Brazilian cryptocurrency exchange Mercado Bitcoin disclosed a major security incident on Nov. 2, 2026, involving approximately $38 million in digital assets. The attack presents a substantial financial and operational challenge for one of Latin America’s largest cryptocurrency platforms, with its re...
content:
Brazilian cryptocurrency exchange Mercado Bitcoin disclosed a major security incident on Nov. 2, 2026, involving approximately $38 million in digital assets. The attack presents a substantial financial and operational challenge for one of Latin America’s largest cryptocurrency platforms, with its response now drawing attention from customers, blockchain investigators, and the broader digital asset industry.

Key Takeaways

  • Mercado Bitcoin’s incident raises concerns about exchange-controlled signing credentials.
  • Mercado Bitcoin suspended platform services while conducting security checks following the attack.
  • Mercado Bitcoin’s recovery depends on more than financial compensation.

Mercado Bitcoin Faces $38 Million Security Crisis

Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin is facing a costly security crisis following a Nov. 2 attack that drained cryptocurrency from its operational wallets. The incident struck one of Latin America’s prominent digital asset platforms, raising immediate questions about the security of exchange-controlled funds and the financial consequences of unauthorized access.

While the company has acknowledged the breach, its response now hinges on containing the damage, establishing the full scope of the intrusion, and demonstrating that its remaining infrastructure can safely support normal operations.

Bitcoin.com News previously reported that Arkham Intelligence analyst Emmett Gallic estimated more than $46 million in suspicious transfers on Monday, exceeding Mercado Bitcoin’s official accounting by at least $8 million. The competing figures have not been publicly reconciled, and it remains unclear whether both assessments encompass identical transactions or asset categories.

Mercado Bitcoin Pledges Customers Will Not Lose Assets

The company sought to calm account holders with an explicit guarantee that they would not bear the financial burden of the incident. “Mercado Bitcoin assures you that you will not suffer any loss of assets due to the security incident we identified today on our platform,” the centralized exchange (CEX) platform’s update explains.

The company’s statement effectively commits the business to making affected users whole, regardless of how much cryptocurrency investigators ultimately recover.

Emergency Shutdown Follows Detection of Suspicious Activity

Mercado Bitcoin identified the occurrence during the early hours of Monday, subsequently suspending deposits, withdrawals, and access to platform services as a preventive measure. The company activated its internal security procedures and reportedly notified the relevant authorities. It also warned users to rely on official communications rather than unsolicited messages or purported support representatives.

The operational interruption affects a business whose customers ordinarily depend on continuous access to cryptocurrency markets, particularly when prices are moving rapidly.

Investigators Scrutinize Compromised Signing Infrastructure

Preliminary analyses suggest attackers obtained control of credentials capable of authorizing transactions, potentially exposing both hot wallets and customer deposit addresses. According to a Bitquery analysis, suspicious activity reportedly spanned chains like Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar, Arbitrum, Tron and Polygon, with some investigators describing unauthorized movements continuing beyond the initial wave of transfers.

Unlike a smart-contract exploit, this suspected compromise concerns access to the mechanisms used to approve legitimate blockchain transactions. Possession of the necessary signing credentials can allow an attacker to move assets without defeating the network’s cryptographic protections. The precise entry point has not been conclusively established.

Tether, Circle and Chainalysis Help Block $11 Million

Mercado Bitcoin enlisted several cryptocurrency companies to restrict assets associated with the breach, securing an initial containment result. “In a swift action with the crypto community and strategic partners—including Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1, and Chainalysis—we have already blocked US$ 11 million,” the exchange stated.

Other amounts eligible for blocking have been identified, according to the company, although it has not provided a definitive figure for additional recoverable assets. Certain centrally issued stablecoins contain administrative functions that permit authorized issuers to prevent token transfers. Native BTC has no comparable issuer-controlled freezing mechanism.

Importantly, restricting stolen tokens does not automatically return them to their previous owners. Subsequent recovery may require cooperation from custodians, legal authorities or other parties controlling the affected assets.

Brazilian Crypto Heavyweight Faces a Defining Test

Founded in 2013, Mercado Bitcoin expanded from a bitcoin brokerage into a diversified financial technology business offering spot trading, staking, tokenized private credit, and payment services. The São Paulo-based company serves approximately 4.5 million to 4.8 million customers and has reported cumulative transaction volume exceeding 215 billion Brazilian reais.

Its expansion attracted a $200 million Softbank investment in 2021, valuing the business at approximately $2.1 billion and establishing it as a Brazilian cryptocurrency unicorn. The exchange has not provided a definitive reopening date. “The resumption of services will take place as soon as full security conditions are in place, and deadlines will be communicated exclusively through our official channels,” the company emphasized.

The remaining challenge is whether Mercado Bitcoin can demonstrate that its security controls have been repaired sufficiently to prevent another intrusion. Financial compensation can address missing balances, but restoring confidence in the systems protecting those balances requires a different kind of proof. The hack comes at a tough time for the crypto industry as it’s been healing its wounds from the latest $6.3 billion Binance hack.

title: NYSE Adds Four Transfer Agents to Planned Tokenized Securities Venue
summary: The New York Stock Exchange said on November 2 that Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate had joined the network supporting its proposed…
content:
TL;DR: The New York Stock Exchange said on November 2 that Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate had joined the network supporting its proposed tokenized securities venue. There is a major distinction between an issuer-sponsored tokenized security and a synthetic token that tracks a stock price without representing an actual company share.

Broadridge separately described plans to provide on-chain governance services, underlining how much of a securities market happens after a trade. Corporate records have to survive splits, dividends, shareholder meetings and ownership disputes. If tokenization ignores those workflows, its speed gains may produce new headaches instead of an easier market.

What the primary source establishes

The New York Stock Exchange said on November 2 that Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate had joined the network supporting its proposed tokenized securities venue. They add to previously announced relationships with Securitize and tZERO. The planned platform is not being presented as a fully operating public marketplace today; a launch depends on further steps, including regulatory approval. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

Transfer agents do the often-invisible work of maintaining official shareholder records and supporting issuer functions. Their participation matters because a token representing a security needs clear ownership, corporate-action handling and investor rights as well as a way to change hands. Putting a token on a ledger does not automatically deliver proxy voting, dividends, reconciliations or legal recognition.

Why this matters beyond the headline

The news shifts tokenization from a discussion of trading speed toward institutional plumbing. The NYSE says the partners collectively have extensive issuer relationships, which could simplify future adoption if product designs are approved. It also suggests that incumbent infrastructure firms are not being bypassed; they are being brought into a possible new recordkeeping and settlement model.

A tokenized instrument must connect technical records with enforceable financial rights. Trading software can move a token quickly, but an issuer, custodian, transfer agent or settlement bank may still have to recognise the result. This is why tokenization announcements need to explain which part of the lifecycle is changing, not merely advertise that a blockchain is involved.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: DTCC’s tokenized securities infrastructure rollout and tokenized fund redemptions tested over a weekend. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

What the announcement does not prove

There is a major distinction between an issuer-sponsored tokenized security and a synthetic token that tracks a stock price without representing an actual company share. The NYSE announcement concerns a planned structure involving regulated participants. It does not establish that a retail customer can buy every listed stock as a 24-hour token immediately or that shareholder rights will be identical under every arrangement.

Real settlement infrastructure is judged by whether it works on bad days, not just during presentations. Reconciliation, asset eligibility, funding, corporate actions and recovery from errors remain central. Continuous technical operation can improve coordination, yet it does not create market liquidity or remove the obligations of regulated participants.

What to watch next

Watch for rule filings, regulatory decisions, supported asset classes, custody standards and the precise rights attached to tokenized shares. Operational details about voting and corporate actions will be as important as the underlying ledger. Until those details emerge, the partnerships demonstrate preparation and potential reach, not completed migration of Wall Street equity trading onto blockchains.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: NEAR Protocol’s House of Stake Votes to Cut Token Issuance 36%
summary: NEAR Protocol’s governance body voted to slash the blockchain’s annual token issuance ceiling by 36%, backing a two-year reduction that promises less dilution for holders but smaller staking rewards for validators and investors helping secure the network over time. NEAR’s House of Stake Backs Lower ...
content:
NEAR Protocol’s governance body voted to slash the blockchain’s annual token issuance ceiling by 36%, backing a two-year reduction that promises less dilution for holders but smaller staking rewards for validators and investors helping secure the network over time.

Key Takeaways

  • NEAR’s House of Stake approved HSP-029 with approximately 99.96% support.
  • SVRN’s CEO proposed a monetary policy change that would reduce future token creation.
  • NEAR validators face tighter economics as staking compensation declines.

NEAR’s House of Stake Backs Lower Token Issuance

On Nov. 2, 2026, NEAR’s House of Stake approved proposal HSP-029 with approximately 99.96% support, representing 3.29 million veNEAR in voting power. The decision advances another monetary policy overhaul for the layer one (L1) blockchain, which previously halved its maximum issuance rate in October 2025.

The latest measure targets a 1.6% annual ceiling, down from 2.5%, through a gradual adjustment spanning 24 months. Each epoch will bring an incremental reduction, averaging 0.0375 percentage points monthly, rather than an abrupt change that catches staking operators flat-footed.

The proposal changes just one protocol parameter. Its existing distribution formula remains intact, allocating 90% of newly minted tokens to staking participants and 10% to the treasury. No additional spending authority accompanies the measure.

SVRN Chief’s Proposal Faces Several Implementation Hurdles

Sal Ternullo, CEO of the Nasdaq-listed SVRN, authored the initiative. His company disclosed holdings of approximately 55 million NEAR, predominantly staked, accounting for more than 8% of the network’s staked supply.

Approval doesn’t immediately activate the adjustment. The House of Stake Security Council must first ratify the result, followed by an approximately 90-day preparation period for exchanges, custodians, wallets, and staking services.

Validators must subsequently implement a protocol upgrade before the scheduled reductions become binding. Quarterly disclosures will compare actual issuance against the published trajectory.

The initiative also follows the withdrawal of a separate Sovereign Fund proposal from NEAR co-founder Illia Polosukhin, who cited risks associated with placing additional responsibilities on the protocol.

Token Supply Savings Come With Lower Staking Yields

Economic modeling accompanying HSP-029 estimates that approximately 11.8 million NEAR in additional issuance would be avoided during the first two years, expanding to 66.1 million over six years compared with maintaining the previous ceiling.

At full implementation, the blockchain network‘s projected daily creation falls from approximately 89,500 tokens to 57,300. However, gross staking yields are expected to decline from 5.268% to 3.372%, assuming participation levels remain comparable.

Validator commission income faces a projected 36% reduction under unchanged conditions, potentially squeezing smaller operators dependent on issuance-based compensation. Non-staking holders, meanwhile, stand to experience slower dilution without sacrificing rewards they weren’t collecting.

NEAR has no fixed maximum supply, although transaction fee burning offsets some emissions. With approximately 1.31 billion tokens circulating, its monetary policy increasingly centers on balancing security incentives against long-term supply growth.

The tension is straightforward. A blockchain protocol can mint fewer tokens, but its validators still need enough economic incentive to keep securing it.

title: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold
summary: Crypto executives expect US regulators to drive crypto policymaking regardless of the midterm election outcome.
content:
With voting underway in the US midterm elections and control of Congress at stake, Maylea Ma, deputy general counsel at 1inch, said she expects federal agencies to drive the next phase of crypto regulation.

The election could reshape the path forward for the stalled CLARITY Act, but Ma said “real movement” in US digital-asset regulation over the next few years will come from the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Treasury, rather than Congress.

Ma said those agencies were increasingly engaging with crypto projects. However, agency engagement does not provide the stability the industry had hoped to secure through legislation.

“The long-term goal, of course, remains a statute that cannot be reversed every time a government changes,” said Ma.

That uncertainty also matters to institutional investors, according to Michael Ho, co-founder of D3, the team behind Doma Protocol.

“With the market structure bill stalled, US crypto policy continues to rest on agency guidance that a future administration can reverse, and that keeps serious capital waiting,” Ho said.

“Whatever the result, clear rules written into law are what will bring institutional capital into tokenized real-world assets.”

In August, the SEC proposed a framework for crypto fundraising, including exemptions for certain token offerings and a safe harbor from treatment as investment contracts. In September, it also updated staff guidance covering token buybacks, crypto networks and staking receipt tokens.

The CFTC, meanwhile, submitted a crypto market regulatory plan for White House review on Sept. 17, two days after the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act.

Related: US midterms election 2026 live coverage

title: Moscow Exchange Confirms Dec. 1 Crypto Trading Launch With Bitcoin, Ether, USDT
summary: Russia’s Moscow Exchange has formally announced plans to begin cryptocurrency trading on Dec. 1, offering bitcoin, ether, and USDT through what it describes as the country’s first organized digital currency market. The exchange confirmed the plans in a Nov. 2 announcement, detailing the trading infr...
content:
Russia’s Moscow Exchange has formally announced plans to begin cryptocurrency trading on Dec. 1, offering bitcoin, ether, and USDT through what it describes as the country’s first organized digital currency market.

Key Takeaways

  • Moscow Exchange plans to launch cryptocurrency trading on December 1, initially supporting bitcoin (BTC), ether (ETH) and USDT, using its existing trading and clearing infrastructure.
  • Retail investors will face restrictions, including mandatory knowledge assessments and annual purchase limits of 300,000 rubles (approximately $3,700) per broker for non-qualified investors.
  • The launch follows an October trading pilot, with Russia seeking to bring crypto activity into regulated markets.

The exchange confirmed the plans in a Nov. 2 announcement, detailing the trading infrastructure, settlement options, and investor restrictions that will accompany the launch. The new market will operate under Russia’s recently enacted cryptocurrency legislation, which took effect on September 1.

Moscow Exchange said the initial rollout will involve pilot transactions, with financial institutions and other participants gaining access as they complete preparations. The exchange reported interest from traditional securities traders, their clients, and businesses already using digital assets for investments and payments.

Trading will take place through the exchange’s existing stock market infrastructure, with transactions processed through the National Clearing Center (NCC). The market will operate from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, matching the exchange’s regular securities trading schedule.

Bitcoin (BTC), ether (ETH), and Tether’s USDT stablecoin will be the first supported assets, with trading offered in both address-based and addressless modes. Moscow Exchange said it intends to expand the selection over time to include additional international cryptocurrencies and Russian digital assets.

The exchange also confirmed that customers will have access to same-day and next-day settlement options, known as TOD and TOM, respectively. Swap transactions will also be available to help market participants manage liquidity.

Retail participation will remain restricted under Russia’s new regulatory framework. Non-qualified investors must pass a knowledge assessment before purchasing cryptocurrencies and will be limited to 300,000 rubles, approximately $3,700, in annual purchases through each broker.

Ready to Launch After Pilot

The announcement builds on preparations previously reported by Bitcoin.com News in October, when Moscow Exchange executive Boris Blokhin revealed that the platform had begun testing cryptocurrency transactions with professional market participants.

Speaking on Oct. 8, Blokhin said the exchange had started its pilot roughly a week earlier and was targeting Dec. 1 for the launch. He also explained that Moscow Exchange could introduce crypto trading using its existing licenses without obtaining additional regulatory approvals.

The initiative represents a significant development in Russia’s efforts to bring cryptocurrency transactions into its regulated financial system, potentially redirecting activity from offshore platforms and informal trading channels.

However, the transition could face challenges. As Bitcoin.com News previously reported, Russian banking giant Sberbank estimated that cryptocurrency trading could reach at least 4 trillion rubles, approximately $46 billion, during the first year of the new regulatory framework.

Despite that substantial projected volume, Sberbank anticipated that only about 20% of transactions would pass through regulated exchanges, with the remainder continuing outside officially supervised markets.

Moscow Exchange’s December launch will provide an early test of whether Russia’s new regulations and established financial institutions can attract a larger share of the country’s cryptocurrency trading activity.

title: BTCPay Server 2.4.7 Security Release Adds Urgency for Self-Hosted Merchants
summary: BTCPay Server’s 2.4.7 release published in late October includes security fixes following a broad review of reported issues.
content:
TL;DR: BTCPay Server’s 2.4.7 release published in late October includes security fixes following a broad review of reported issues. Disclosure of a serious issue is not proof that it has been exploited in the wild.

The appeal of self-hosting is genuine control over funds and infrastructure. The hidden cost is that responsibility cannot be outsourced to a hosted provider’s security team. For small merchants, having a routine patch window and recovery procedure can be more valuable than sophisticated features they never have time to maintain.

What the primary source establishes

BTCPay Server’s 2.4.7 release published in late October includes security fixes following a broad review of reported issues. The project’s release materials describe findings across several severities. That makes the update relevant to businesses operating their own Bitcoin payment servers, particularly hosts that manage multiple merchants or expose administrative functions to the internet. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

A self-hosted payment processor reduces dependence on an intermediary, but it does not remove the responsibilities of software operations. Administrators must handle updates, backups, access permissions, plugin compatibility and infrastructure monitoring. A vulnerability in payout handling or account permissions can be especially serious when a server is shared by multiple organisations.

Why this matters beyond the headline

The story is less about a dramatic exploit claim than about maintenance discipline. A security advisory gives operators something concrete to act on: identify the version running, review the release notes and apply the upgrade through a tested process. The goal is to fix known weaknesses without creating avoidable downtime or losing merchant configuration.

A crypto incident produces several separate timelines: containment, investigation, recovery and a return to reliable service. Those phases can overlap without finishing together. A traced wallet is not automatically frozen; a frozen balance is not automatically returned; and a reopened withdrawal route is not a completed security audit. Keeping those differences visible helps readers judge progress more accurately.

For additional perspective, it is worth reading our existing reporting on Binance’s earlier staged withdrawal restart and Bitcoin payment infrastructure and node software context. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

What the announcement does not prove

Disclosure of a serious issue is not proof that it has been exploited in the wild. Nor does an updated application automatically secure an outdated operating system, compromised administrator account or badly configured plugin. Teams should separate the product patch from other elements of their threat model and avoid promising complete protection after one version change.

Operational controls matter most when a business is under stress. Security announcements should identify the system affected, the customers who can act, the evidence supporting any recovery number and what remains uncertain. Clear scope protects users from false reassurance and from unnecessary panic. It also provides a sensible basis for follow-up accountability.

What to watch next

Operators should review the official release page for the precise upgrade guidance, create verified backups and check post-update payment and payout flows. Where merchants share infrastructure, permission boundaries deserve explicit testing. Customers should not be told payments are secure solely because a version number changed; sensible monitoring remains necessary.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: RUNE rallies 15% as THORChain restarts most swaps after halt
summary: THORChain has restored trading on Bitcoin, Ethereum and several other networks following a refund bug, while three chains remain paused.
content:
THORChain’s RUNE token rose about 15% over the past 24 hours as the cross-chain swap protocol restored trading on most networks following a weekend halt triggered by an Ethereum block reorganization.

THORChain (RUNE) was trading at around $0.64 on Wednesday, up approximately 15% over the previous day, according to CoinMarketCap.

THORChain’s network status page showed trading and transaction signing marked “OK” on 10 of its 13 listed external networks. BNB Smart Chain, Cosmos Hub and Solana continued to show warnings for both functions.

Bitcoin, Ethereum, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin, Litecoin, Tron and Zcash were among the networks showing trading was re-enabled. Avalanche, Base and XRP were already operating when Cointelegraph reported on the halt on Monday.

Ethereum reorg exposed refund bug

The disruption began on Saturday when a one-block Ethereum reorganization removed a 10 Ether deposit that THORChain had already credited, according to the protocol’s account.

After the swap failed to meet its price limit, THORChain issued a refund against funds its vault had never received. The sender’s actual deposit was also refunded, resulting in an extra 10 ETH payout and triggering an automatic pause.

Node operators subsequently paused trading across multiple networks while developers investigated.

The halt also disrupted attempts to move funds stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to blockchain analytics company Chainalysis, which said the pause had inadvertently delayed laundering by North Korean hackers.

The partial restart restores access to several cross-chain swap routes.

Related: THORChain halts swaps after block reorg bug, slowing Binance hackers

title: Tron Founder Justin Sun Seeks Sanctions Against Trump-Backed World Liberty Financial
summary: Tron founder Justin Sun is seeking nearly $264,000 in sanctions against World Liberty Financial and its attorneys, accusing the Trump family-backed cryptocurrency company of withholding information about its United Arab Emirates ownership ties until months into a lawsuit over his frozen WLFI tokens....
content:
Tron founder Justin Sun is seeking nearly $264,000 in sanctions against World Liberty Financial and its attorneys, accusing the Trump family-backed cryptocurrency company of withholding information about its United Arab Emirates ownership ties until months into a lawsuit over his frozen WLFI tokens.

Key Takeaways

  • Tron founder Justin Sun is seeking $263,821 in sanctions against World Liberty Financial and its attorneys, alleging the company concealed its UAE ownership ties during litigation over his frozen WLFI tokens.
  • Sun claims World Liberty initially disclosed only Florida citizenship before revealing 22 individuals and entities in its ownership chain, including UAE connections, shortly after a federal judge questioned its efforts to move the case into private arbitration.
  • Sun’s attorneys argue the delayed disclosure wasted months of litigation and undermined federal jurisdiction, forcing the case toward California state court.

Sun Seeks Sanctions

In a motion filed Monday in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, Sun and two affiliated companies alleged that World Liberty submitted inaccurate corporate disclosures that allowed the parties to spend months litigating a dispute the federal court may have lacked jurisdiction to hear.

Sun highlighted the filing in a Tuesday post on X, accusing World Liberty of revealing its foreign ownership connections only after a judge questioned the company’s efforts to move the dispute into private arbitration.

The filing traces the controversy to June 2, when World Liberty submitted a disclosure identifying Florida as its only state of citizenship. However, an amended filing submitted August 26 identified 22 individuals and entities in the company’s ownership chain, with citizenship extending to Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.

That disclosure could defeat federal jurisdiction because Sun and his co-plaintiffs are foreign parties, while World Liberty is also considered a foreign citizen for jurisdictional purposes through its ownership structure.

According to the motion, the timing was particularly troubling because the revised disclosure came six days after an Aug. 20 hearing at which U.S. District Judge James Donato challenged World Liberty’s argument that all of Sun’s claims belonged in arbitration.

Sun’s attorneys contend that World Liberty’s amended disclosure effectively derailed months of litigation after the company encountered resistance to its arbitration arguments, alleging that the “timing… smacks of gamesmanship.” They argue that World Liberty and its lawyers should have identified the relevant ownership information before submitting their original disclosure.

World Liberty’s attorneys previously said they had only recently learned of the additional citizenship information. Sun’s lawyers subsequently requested documents, a deposition, and explanations of how the original disclosure was prepared.

According to the filing, World Liberty produced limited documentation, but declined to provide a deposition or details about its lawyers’ investigation into the company’s ownership structure.

Sun’s attorneys are requesting $263,821.20 in legal fees and costs incurred while opposing World Liberty’s arbitration motion. The amount covers work performed by four lawyers at Cahill Gordon & Reindel and excludes additional legal expenses incurred by other attorneys.

The motion seeks sanctions under the court’s inherent authority and a federal statute governing attorneys who unreasonably prolong litigation. A hearing is scheduled for December 10.

Justin Sun vs. Trump’s Crypto Company

The dispute stems from Sun’s April 21 lawsuit alleging that World Liberty fraudulently induced him to purchase tens of millions of dollars in WLFI tokens under a November 2024 agreement, before improperly freezing his holdings and restricting his governance rights.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, Sun alleged that the company used a smart contract function to freeze approximately 2.9 billion WLFI tokens. World Liberty defended its restrictions as security measures intended to protect the platform.

The conflict escalated further in May when World Liberty filed a separate defamation lawsuit against Sun, accusing him of spreading misleading claims and engaging in trading activities intended to damage WLFI’s market value. Sun denied those allegations.

The newly disputed UAE connections also come amid wider scrutiny of World Liberty’s international financial relationships, including separate litigation involving a reported $500 million UAE-backed investment and transactions involving the project’s USD1 stablecoin.

Sun’s attorneys say the federal case will need to be refiled in California state court because of the jurisdictional issue. However, they argue the federal judge can still impose sanctions for conduct that occurred before dismissal.

“I will keep fighting for the transparency this community deserves,” Sun wrote on X regarding the filing.

Bitcoin.com News reached out to World Liberty Financial for comment on Sun’s latest move in the case, and will update this story if a response is sent.

title: Aave Freezes New tBTC Supply and Borrowing After Mint-and-Redeem Pause
summary: Aave contributors said the protocol had frozen additional tBTC supply and borrowing in its Ethereum Core market after Threshold’s temporary pause of the…
content:
TL;DR: Aave contributors said the protocol had frozen additional tBTC supply and borrowing in its Ethereum Core market after Threshold’s temporary pause of the token’s mint-and-redeem functions. It would be misleading to conclude that tBTC has lost its Bitcoin backing solely because mint and redemption were paused.

This case demonstrates why collateral quality is more complicated than an asset ticker. A wrapped token can track the price of Bitcoin under normal conditions yet carry an extra dependency on bridges, custodians and redemption operations. Lending protocols have to manage those risks separately from the volatility of the underlying coin.

What the primary source establishes

Aave contributors said the protocol had frozen additional tBTC supply and borrowing in its Ethereum Core market after Threshold’s temporary pause of the token’s mint-and-redeem functions. The Aave response was activated on October 31. The restriction is specific to that asset and market; the notice did not describe a blanket freeze of unrelated Aave lending pools. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

Wrapped Bitcoin assets represent claims or accounting mechanisms that connect Bitcoin exposure to another chain. If the mint or redemption bridge is temporarily unavailable, liquidity can change even while the token continues to trade. Lending markets react by limiting new positions that might increase risk, while allowing existing debt repayment and collateral withdrawal subject to normal account health.

Why this matters beyond the headline

An important point for borrowers is that pausing new tBTC activity does not itself change the liquidation threshold. Existing users can still face liquidation if collateral values or borrowing positions move enough to breach their health requirements. That is why a precautionary freeze and a liquidation event should not be treated as synonyms.

Decentralised lending introduces risk factors that are easy to miss if readers focus only on collateral prices. Market parameters, oracle design, token wrappers, governance powers and liquidity all affect what a user can actually do. Restrictions can reduce new exposure while leaving existing accounts sensitive to market movements. The correct interpretation starts with the exact affected pool and the functions that remain available.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: Aave’s first externally curated V4 lending markets and Aave’s proposed liquidation-related safeguards. They explain related market structure and should not be mistaken for evidence that every new proposal is already live.

What the announcement does not prove

It would be misleading to conclude that tBTC has lost its Bitcoin backing solely because mint and redemption were paused. The governance discussion describes a protective response to a specific operating condition, not a definitive finding of insolvency or fraud. The impact on an individual position depends on its collateral mix, borrowed assets and access to market liquidity.

A protocol may be automated, but its risk policy still has to be defined and maintained by people. New assets bring new dependencies; bridges and wrapped tokens add operational points of failure. Users need clear information about repayment, collateral withdrawal and liquidation conditions. Without that detail, a statement about “pausing DeFi” can be almost meaningless.

What to watch next

Watch Threshold’s official timeline for restoring mint and redemption, liquidity conditions for tBTC and any Aave governance proposal to amend market parameters. Users with existing positions should read the precise market notice rather than rely on headlines about a “DeFi freeze”. Clear, asset-specific communication is particularly important when markets move faster than governance procedures.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, prediction markets favored Democrats taking control of Congress as Americans headed to the polls for the US midterm elections, Kraken restricted accounts linked to a suspected $133 million crypto theft in Europe, and North Korea denied involvement in the $6.3 billion Binance hack.

US midterms: Prediction markets favor Democrats in key crypto races

As Americans across the country head to the polls for the US midterm elections Tuesday, prediction market traders have spent months wagering on the outcome. According to an analysis by The Washington Post, nearly $1.9 billion in election-related contracts had traded on Kalshi and Polymarket as of Monday, marking record trading activity for a midterm election cycle.

Markets on both platforms favor Democrats winning control of Congress, with a Democratic sweep priced at 75% on Kalshi and 75.5% on Polymarket as of 4:30 pm UTC. Kalshi traders gave Democrats a 93% chance of taking the House and a 75% chance of winning the Senate, while Polymarket priced those outcomes at 94.5% and 75.5%, respectively.

The vote comes nine days after prediction markets failed to anticipate the outcome of Brazil’s presidential election, with Flávio Bolsonaro favored at roughly 80% the day before incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the runoff. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour reportedly cautioned that “a 5% probability doesn’t mean it won’t happen,” according to CNBC.

For the crypto industry, a shift in congressional control could reshape the prospects for long-awaited regulatory clarity.

“This wasn’t one mistake or one breach — it was a months-long campaign,” Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in a Tuesday post on X.

Kraken restricts accounts amid suspected $133M EU crypto theft

Kraken has restricted accounts linked to a suspected crypto theft of more than $133 million from an unidentified European Union entity and is working with law enforcement to support recovery efforts.

“This incident did not originate on the Kraken platform, and we’re actively investigating reports that some of the assets were subsequently moved through accounts on our platform,” Kraken told Cointelegraph. “We’ve restricted the accounts in question and are working with law enforcement to support recovery efforts.”

Kraken’s statement follows blockchain investigator ZachXBT’s disclosure on Tuesday that he identified another $27 million in withdrawals from centralized exchanges, increasing the suspected losses from the $106 million he reported on Monday. He said some withdrawals occurred after his initial disclosure.

Bitquery reported that the suspected stolen funds were withdrawn from accounts at Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX. It also found that $62.98 million in stablecoins was converted into 27,553 Ether (ETH) within roughly four hours.

Crypto.com told Cointelegraph that it had taken steps to prevent funds associated with the incident from moving through its platform.

OKX acknowledged Cointelegraph’s request for comment and said it was looking into the matter.

North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US

Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denied North Korea’s involvement in the $6.3 billion Binance hack and appeared to suggest, without evidence, that the US could have been behind the theft.

In a statement released via the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on Tuesday, Kim rejected the FBI’s attribution of the attack to a North Korean-backed hacking group.

“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a ‘cyber criminal state’, claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” said Kim. “But the US assertion is an absurd rhetoric and nothing new.”

She described the allegations as a political provocation intended to damage North Korea’s international standing. The FBI also blamed North Korea for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, an accusation Kim also rejected on Tuesday.

“This is not the first time that the U.S. has attempted to spread misunderstanding of the DPRK in the international community, blindly linking the DPRK with the ‘cyber crime’ incidents whenever they occur on an international scale,” said Kim.
