title: Binance Inflows Flip Positive After $7 Billion Post-Hack Exodus
summary: Binance’s tracked wallets have swung back to roughly $3.25 billion in 24-hour net inflows after recording more than $7 billion in daily outflows following its $6.3 billion hack. Binance Users Return as 24-Hour Inflows Swing Positive Money is starting to flow back into Binance after one of the larges...
content:
Binance’s tracked wallets have swung back to roughly $3.25 billion in 24-hour net inflows after recording more than $7 billion in daily outflows following its $6.3 billion hack.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance swung back to positive 24-hour net inflows after post-hack outflows topped $7 billion daily.
  • Weekly net outflows still stand near $12 billion, showing confidence has not fully recovered.
  • Sustained deposits after withdrawals normalize will reveal whether Binance has truly stabilized.

Binance Users Return as 24-Hour Inflows Swing Positive

Money is starting to flow back into Binance after one of the largest security shocks in crypto history.

Binance recorded about $3.25 billion in 24-hour net inflows according to Defillama data, as of this writing, reversing the heavy withdrawals that followed the Oct. 29 hack. The exchange’s tracked onchain assets stood at roughly $128.8 billion.

“By 03:00 UTC [Nov 3], we are seeing hourly deposits exceed withdrawals,” Binance said earlier Tuesday, describing the shift as a sign of stabilizing user activity.

$12 Billion Weekly Drain Shows Trust Is Not Fully Restored

One positive day does not erase the damage.

Defillama still showed approximately $12.16 billion in seven-day net outflows and $10.85 billion over 30 days. The rolling figures can change quickly as large transfers enter and leave the measurement window.

Binance’s own shorter-term data earlier Tuesday showed $10.97 billion in withdrawals against $5.70 billion in deposits during the first 46 hours after withdrawals began reopening, leaving a $5.28 billion deficit over that period.

Co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao said only a small share of withdrawals appeared to move to rival centralized exchanges (CEXs). He wrote on X:

According to public reports, only 6-10% of withdrawals went to other CEX. Majority went to self-custody wallets, and have not interacted with a DEX yet. Stay safe.

Yi He Details North Korea-Linked Threat Attempts

Binance paused withdrawals for security checks after the breach before reopening them in phases and expanding support to more assets. Co-founder Yi He said the incident came against a persistent backdrop of attempted state-sponsored attacks.

“Throughout 2026, Binance’s security team detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases,” Yi He wrote on X.

She said the tactics included fraudulent job interviews, malicious developer tools, compromised software packages, browser extensions, fake video-conferencing apps, and social-engineering campaigns designed to steal credentials or deploy remote-access malware.

“We intercepted many of them, but the cost of failing to stop even one was severe, and this should never have happened,” she said.

U.S. officials have linked the Oct. 29 attack to a North Korean group, an accusation Pyongyang has denied. Kim Yo Jong has separately questioned the U.S. attribution and pointed to Washington’s policy of confiscating stolen bitcoin.

Positive Inflows Become Binance’s First Confidence Test

Binance said it covered customer losses with its own resources and resumed withdrawals after security checks. Co-CEO Richard Teng said the exchange was beginning to see “more positive inflows,” while the return of deposits provides the first measurable sign that immediate panic may be fading.

Still, the weekly figures argue for caution.

For Binance, the next test is not whether deposits can exceed withdrawals for several hours. It is whether users continue returning once services fully normalize and the initial shock disappears.

After billions rushed out, sustained positive flows would offer much stronger evidence that confidence in the world’s largest crypto exchange is actually being rebuilt.

title: BitMine Reports 6.06M ETH Holdings, With More Than 5.22M Staked
summary: BitMine Immersion Technologies reported holdings of 6,060,506 ETH as of November 1 in a November 2 filing exhibit.
content:
TL;DR: BitMine Immersion Technologies reported holdings of 6,060,506 ETH as of November 1 in a November 2 filing exhibit. Cryptocurrency balance sheets are sensitive to valuation dates.

The filing’s detailed token count is valuable precisely because it can be compared with later disclosures. It also exposes a blind spot in quick “ETH treasury” comparisons: two companies with identical token balances could have very different liquidity, financing and operational risk. Staking arrangements are an essential part of that distinction.

What the primary source establishes

BitMine Immersion Technologies reported holdings of 6,060,506 ETH as of November 1 in a November 2 filing exhibit. The company said 5,227,037 ETH were staked, alongside smaller Bitcoin holdings, cash and other positions. These are issuer-disclosed balances at a specified date, not independently observed live holdings or a claim about Ethereum’s total currently liquid supply. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

Staking means committing ETH to help secure Ethereum’s proof-of-stake network through validators or staking arrangements. Rewards depend on protocol conditions and operating choices, while access to staked assets can involve withdrawal queues or third-party arrangements. A substantial staked position may produce ongoing reward income, but it is not equivalent to holding the same amount in immediately transferable cash.

Why this matters beyond the headline

BitMine’s size makes its liquidity choices important. A large corporate ETH owner may hold a long-term position, but the market will still examine potential issuance, borrowing, staking income and the ability to rebalance. The issuer says its holdings represent a notable share of ETH’s supply; the comparison is a company calculation and should be tied to the supply and price assumptions used.

Ethereum has multiple sources of demand and risk: trading, staking, stablecoin settlement, application fees and long-term treasury allocation. A change in one part of that system should be tested against the others instead of promoted into a universal explanation. The market often overreacts when one publicly available metric is mistaken for the whole network economy.

For additional perspective, it is worth reading our existing reporting on BitMine’s earlier ETH accumulation and staking disclosure and our Ethereum market reporting. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

What the announcement does not prove

Cryptocurrency balance sheets are sensitive to valuation dates. A dollar figure derived from the company’s ETH price assumption can change materially without any coins moving. Staking rewards should also be separated from share-price performance and company operating costs. A large token position does not by itself tell shareholders whether their ownership is increasing or being diluted.

For investors, the right comparison is between liquidity, expected holding period and obligations. Staked ETH, ETF shares and treasury holdings may all track the same underlying asset, but their exit routes and operating constraints differ. A useful report therefore asks not simply how much ETH is involved, but how readily the exposure can be changed when conditions deteriorate.

What to watch next

Look for future reports distinguishing unstaked liquidity, locked or queued balances, reward income, cash uses and equity issuance. Those measures will tell investors more about treasury resilience than the headline ETH number alone. For Ethereum, the interesting network question is whether institutional-sized staking concentrations affect how observers assess operator diversity and risk.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: SpaceX blocks tokenized stock listing on OKXICE despite offshore trading boom
summary: SpaceX joined several other issuers objecting to OKXICE tokenized trading, months after crypto platforms offered tokens tied to its shares.
content:
Just months after tokenized versions of SpaceX shares became one of the biggest drivers of onchain stock trading, the aerospace company is pushing back against plans to bring similar trading to US investors.

According to a Nov. 2 public notice from OKXICE, SpaceX has objected to the proposed listing of tokenized versions of its shares on the trading venue, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). The company now joins Tesla and Amazon among 56 companies objecting to the proposed listings.

Under the Securities and Exchange Commission’s five-year Innovation Exemption introduced in September, platforms such as OKXICE can offer trading in tokenized versions of US stocks without registering as national securities exchanges. But the framework also gives companies a say in the process: They have 30 days to object to the proposed trading of their shares tokenized by third parties, effectively keeping those tokens off the venue.

Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based representations of company shares that allow investors to gain exposure to traditional equities onchain, often around the clock. Depending on the structure, they can be backed by actual shares, although the rights granted to tokenholders may differ from those of traditional shareholders.

OKXICE co-chair and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo told Cointelegraph on Oct. 20 that the venture expected more objections as companies avoided being the first to test the model. 

SpaceX’s objection comes despite tokenized versions of its shares already trading on platforms outside the US, where they have attracted significant trading activity since the company’s June public offering.

Offshore trading since June

Ahead of the SpaceX listing, Backpack Securities, a stock brokerage and tokenization platform, and crypto exchange Kraken, through its xStocks offering, both prepared tokenized versions of the aerospace company’s stock, each designed to be backed by actual shares. Backpack’s SPCX token went on to record $1.08 billion in onchain trading volume in June, while Kraken’s SPCXx token recorded $852 million.

Unlike Backpack and Kraken, OKXICE would open tokenized stock trading to US investors under the SEC’s new regulatory framework, potentially tapping into the world’s largest equity market by capitalization and expanding the investor base for tokenized securities.

Nasdaq warned issuers in September that they “must be cautious about their participation” in the venture, arguing that tokenized stock trading could fragment liquidity and undermine long-term shareholder value.

Despite the growing opposition, Cuomo said during an Oct. 30 press conference that as people see the benefits of tokenization, “you’ll see more and more companies participate.”

title: October’s Dormant Bitcoin Awakenings Cool as Transfers Plunge 81% From August
summary: Dormant bitcoin wallets dating back to 2012 moved 2,159.15 BTC valued at $167.56 million last month, marking a second consecutive monthly slowdown. Despite the declining activity, wallets originating in 2013 dominated the month, while addresses from Bitcoin’s earliest years remained conspicuously ab...
content:
Dormant bitcoin wallets dating back to 2012 moved 2,159.15 BTC valued at $167.56 million last month, marking a second consecutive monthly slowdown. Despite the declining activity, wallets originating in 2013 dominated the month, while addresses from Bitcoin’s earliest years remained conspicuously absent.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s dormant wallet activity declined for a second consecutive month.
  • Btcparser tracked 35 October transfers, with large transactions dominating the totals.
  • Bitcoin addresses established in 2010 and 2011 were absent from October’s records.

Dormant Bitcoin Activity Slows as 35 Transfers Move $167 Million

October brought another round of long-sleeping bitcoin wallets back to life, but the action was considerably quieter than the fireworks witnessed in August and September. Between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, btcparser.com tracked 35 transfers involving 2,159.15 BTC, worth approximately $167.56 million using a reference price of $77,606 per coin.

The month’s biggest transaction came on Oct. 20, when a wallet established Jan. 23, 2016, moved a whopping 500 BTC valued at $38.80 million. Yet that blockbuster transfer concealed a broader retreat in dormant bitcoin spending.

October’s Dormant Bitcoin Transfers Fall Sharply From August

The figures show a pronounced cooldown from August’s 6,427.59 BTC across 188 transfers and September’s 5,419.45 BTC through 94 movements. October’s bitcoin volume dropped roughly 66% from August and 60% from September, while transaction counts contracted even more sharply.

July, however, was quieter still, with 30 transfers totaling 1,264.16 BTC. October’s average transaction reached 61.69 BTC, exceeding the previous three months despite its substantially smaller overall volume.

The October activity was anything but evenly distributed. Between Oct. 17 and Oct. 21, just 10 transfers accounted for 1,620.75 BTC, or approximately three-quarters of the month’s total. Four transactions alone moved 1,361.21 BTC, valued at $105.64 million.

Bitcoin Wallets From 2013 Take Center Stage

Addresses first funded in 2013 stole the show, accounting for 993.61 BTC worth $77.11 million across 11 transfers. That represented 46.02% of October’s bitcoin volume, compared with approximately 16% in September and 13% in August.

The 2016 cohort ranked second with 546.95 BTC, followed by 2017 addresses with 355.93 BTC. Wallets established in 2014 contributed 174.46 BTC, a far cry from August’s 3,286.26 BTC attributed to that vintage.

One particularly intriguing pairing occurred Oct. 17, when two 2013 wallets transferred 248.85 BTC and 167.84 BTC just five seconds apart within block 971894. Their synchronized timing suggests possible common control, although the blockchain evidence alone cannot establish shared ownership.

October’s Biggest Day Packs a $39 Million Wallop

Oct. 20 packed the heaviest punch, with 511.20 BTC moving in a single day, worth approximately $39.67 million. That same date also witnessed activity from the oldest address in the dataset, established Feb. 14, 2012, which transferred 11.2 BTC after more than 14 years. Another noteworthy detail involved two wallets created on consecutive Christmas dates in 2015. Both transferred exactly 10 BTC on Oct. 23, with their movements separated by eight minutes.

The smallest transactions were comparatively modest, including three transfers below 0.01 BTC. Such activity depends partly on btcparser.com’s detection criteria and should not be interpreted as a complete accounting of every older bitcoin address spending coins.

Bitcoin’s Earliest Wallets Go Quiet

Perhaps the most telling absence involved addresses originating in 2010 and 2011. Neither vintage appeared in October’s dataset, following September’s 600 BTC attributed to 2010 wallets alone. The latest figures capture spending from selected dormant addresses rather than verified sales, meaning the coins could have been transferred between wallets controlled by the same holder.

The four-month sleeping bitcoin movement total from July through October 2026 was 15,270.35 BTC, worth approximately $1.185 billion using current BTC exchange rates. With October’s activity concentrated in a handful of hefty transactions, the lingering mystery isn’t simply how much bitcoin moved. It’s whether these aging holdings are changing hands or merely changing to newer bitcoin addresses.

title: Strategy Adds 811 Bitcoin and Repurchases $208.2M of STRC Shares
summary: Strategy announced on November 2 that it had acquired another 811 Bitcoin for roughly $65.5 million and repurchased approximately $208.2 million of its…
content:
TL;DR: Strategy announced on November 2 that it had acquired another 811 Bitcoin for roughly $65.5 million and repurchased approximately $208.2 million of its STRC preferred shares. The dollar amounts are those disclosed by Strategy for the specified transactions.

The timing is notable because the company had separately disclosed large Bitcoin holdings at the end of October. A new acquisition can be checked against that earlier snapshot, but readers should not merge numbers from different dates without adjustment. Preferred-stock capital structure is less eye-catching than the coin count, yet it can be decisive when market conditions change.

What the primary source establishes

Strategy announced on November 2 that it had acquired another 811 Bitcoin for roughly $65.5 million and repurchased approximately $208.2 million of its STRC preferred shares. The disclosure combines two very different capital-allocation decisions: increasing BTC holdings and reducing a class of outstanding preferred equity. Investors should assess both parts rather than treat the announcement as a simple Bitcoin purchase notice. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

Purchasing Bitcoin increases the company’s direct exposure to the asset. Repurchasing preferred shares changes the number of securities outstanding and can affect financing obligations, investor returns and how management uses available capital. STRC is not common equity, so its buyback has different implications from repurchasing ordinary shares; the security’s terms and price matter.

Why this matters beyond the headline

Treasury-company headlines often focus on how many coins were added, but financing costs help determine whether that strategy creates durable shareholder value. The simultaneous buyback is a useful reminder that a Bitcoin-heavy balance sheet must still be funded and managed. If new securities are issued at one point and repurchased later, the relevant comparison involves proceeds, purchase prices and future distributions.

Fund flows and corporate Bitcoin holdings share one characteristic: they are easy to count and harder to interpret. A securities wrapper reports its own creations and redemptions; a public company reports transactions inside a particular capital structure. Neither dataset captures every spot-market participant. A useful analysis establishes the reporting date, identifies what was measured and asks how much the disclosed activity represents relative to the wider market.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: Strategy’s earlier capital-management review and the company’s expanded Bitcoin financing framework. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

What the announcement does not prove

The dollar amounts are those disclosed by Strategy for the specified transactions. They do not, on their own, establish the company’s total current market value, future BTC acquisitions or returns to every class of shareholder. Nor should an accounting gain on Bitcoin be treated as cash generated by ordinary operations without looking at the underlying financial statements.

The critical operational issue is access to liquid Bitcoin exposure. A fund shareholder may own a listed security, while a corporate treasury holder owns shares in a company with liabilities and management decisions. Those two instruments can behave differently even when Bitcoin is the most visible asset behind both. Treating the wrapper as identical to the coin erases meaningful risks.

What to watch next

Next, monitor additional regulatory filings, financing terms and the ratio of Bitcoin acquisitions to securities issuance or retirement. For a business whose public narrative is built around BTC accumulation, the balance-sheet mechanics are increasingly part of the investment thesis. The quantity of Bitcoin is clear; the economic cost of obtaining and maintaining that exposure takes more work to understand.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

summary:
Polymarket has
received approval from the National Futures Association for its affiliated
entity, PM Derivatives, LLC, to operate as a Futures Commission Merchant. The
broker will operate on a fully collateralised basis, requiring customers to
fund their positions in full at the time of each trade.
...
content:
2026-11-03T22:26:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 03/11/2026 | 20:26 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • PM Derivatives will accept and carry customer orders and funds, with all positions fully collateralised at trade entry.
  • The registration gives Polymarket another regulated route to work with distribution partners and expand into certain jurisdictions.

Polymarket has received approval from the National Futures Association for its affiliated entity, PM Derivatives, LLC, to operate as a Futures Commission Merchant. The broker will operate on a fully collateralised basis, requiring customers to fund their positions in full at the time of each trade.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The approval comes amid continued regulatory scrutiny of prediction markets in the US. In August, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission warned regulated firms against using American-style bookmaker odds to list, solicit or advertise derivatives.

It said prices should instead be displayed in nominal or percentage terms that reflect market pricing, warning that bookmaker-style formats could mislead customers about the nature of the contracts.

Polymarket Completes Three-Part US Derivatives Structure

The registration completes three key components of Polymarket's US derivatives infrastructure: an exchange, a clearinghouse and a broker. Each function operates through a separate affiliated entity.

QCX LLC, doing business as Polymarket US, operates the exchange , while QC Clearing LLC serves as the clearinghouse. PM Derivatives will handle the brokerage function.

Its FCM status adds an intermediated layer to Polymarket's existing direct exchange model. The registration allows PM Derivatives to accept and carry customer orders and funds as a broker, subject to CFTC and NFA requirements.

— News Gurus🦉 (@NewsGurus) November 3, 2026

Polymarket Keeps Existing Partners Alongside New FCM

It also provides Polymarket with another regulated route to work with distribution partners. This could support its expansion into jurisdictions where access to derivatives markets requires a partnership with a regulated broker.

PM Derivatives will initially operate exclusively on a fully collateralised basis. Any future offering of margin services would require additional regulatory approval, according to the company.

The registration will not replace Polymarket's existing brokerage arrangements. The company will continue working with its current FCM and brokerage partners, which will retain access to Polymarket US markets for their own customers.

title: CFTC clears stock perpetual futures for trading on US exchanges
summary: US regulators are opening the door to stock-based perpetual futures, extending a popular crypto trading product into traditional markets amid ongoing legal disputes.
content:
Perpetual futures contracts tied to individual stocks can begin trading on regulated US exchanges for the first time, according to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), extending a derivatives product popularized in cryptocurrency markets into traditional equities.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said in a Tuesday statement that the contracts were deemed approved under CFTC Regulation 40.3 and could be offered on exchanges registered with both the CFTC and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to trade security futures products.

Selig said bringing the products into regulated US markets would allow American traders to access perpetual futures under US regulatory safeguards rather than being “forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues.”

Perpetual futures allow traders to take positions on an asset’s price without owning the underlying asset or facing an expiration date. Crypto exchange BitMEX helped popularize the instruments, commonly referred to as perps, in 2016.

CFTC announces approval of equity perpetual futures trading. Source: CFTC

The announcement follows a wave of regulatory filings in September, when Coinbase, Kalshi and Kraken parent Payward, through its Bitnomial exchange, sought approval to offer perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. OG.com joined the push days later, proposing contracts that could trade around the clock on weekdays.

The filings followed the CFTC’s May approval of Bitcoin perpetual futures contracts for Kalshi and separate regulatory relief allowing Coinbase to provide access to certain cryptocurrency perpetual futures listed on an affiliated foreign exchange.

Selig did not identify which exchanges would offer the contracts or provide a timeline for when trading would begin.

Related: CFTC sues Utah to block action against prediction markets 

US push for perpetual futures faces legal challenge

The announcement also comes nearly three months after President Donald Trump said the CFTC was working to bring Hyperliquid, a decentralized crypto exchange best known for its perpetual futures trading, into the US in a “fully compliant and legal fashion.”

Trump made the remarks during an Aug. 19 White House event. At the time, neither the CFTC nor Hyperliquid had announced a formal plan for bringing the platform to US markets.

However, the CFTC’s approach to perpetual futures has faced legal opposition. In June, CME Group’s Chicago Mercantile Exchange sued the regulator over its approval of cryptocurrency perpetual futures, arguing that the contracts should be regulated as swaps rather than futures and that the agency had exceeded its authority. The distinction matters because swaps are subject to different regulatory requirements, potentially including stricter reporting, margin and registration rules, while futures can trade under the existing futures exchange framework.

The CFTC moved to dismiss the lawsuit in September, arguing that CME lacked standing because it had not demonstrated financial harm and could list similar contracts itself.

Wall Street group challenges CFTC approval

Meanwhile, the Capital Markets Alliance, a coalition that includes Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets, filed a lawsuit Tuesday afternoon seeking to overturn the CFTC’s approval.

The group argues that the contracts are security-based swaps under the SEC’s jurisdiction and that the CFTC violated the Administrative Procedure Act by failing to adequately explain its decision or consider the potential impact on investors. The lawsuit also seeks to prevent the approvals from taking effect while the case proceeds.

title: Tether Says It Froze More Than $1.5B Linked to the Binance Theft
summary: Tether said on November 2 that it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT linked to the late-October Binance attack, working with investigators and…
content:
TL;DR: Tether said on November 2 that it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT linked to the late-October Binance attack, working with investigators and industry partners. Tether’s announcement gives the company’s account of its involvement; it does not independently establish the ultimate ownership or recoverability of every frozen token.

It is tempting to present freezing power as either an unqualified feature or a fatal flaw. The more useful comparison is with the protections and limits users expect from banks and payment providers. In both worlds, legal compliance can restrict access, yet the remedy process and transparency of decisions matter just as much as the initial intervention.

What the primary source establishes

Tether said on November 2 that it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT linked to the late-October Binance attack, working with investigators and industry partners. The company said it moved quickly after receiving actionable intelligence. The claim describes issuer-enforced restrictions on specified token balances; a freeze is not the same thing as completed asset recovery or money already returned to victims. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

Centralised stablecoins can include smart-contract functions that allow the issuer to block transfers by designated addresses. This gives law-enforcement partners a tool that does not exist in the same form for native Bitcoin. But it also makes a particular promise implicit in the product: the ability to transact depends in part on an issuer retaining authority over the transfer rules.

Why this matters beyond the headline

The case illustrates a genuine trade-off. The power to immobilise suspected stolen funds may increase the chance that investigators preserve value while they work. The same central control raises questions about mistaken identification, appeals, transparency and the geographic reach of private restrictions. Stablecoins are often used because they feel like simple digital dollars, yet their governance can be as consequential as their transaction speed.

The phrase “digital dollar” can obscure important differences between products. A stablecoin holder faces an issuer and its reserve arrangements; an exchange user faces trading and custody arrangements; a merchant faces conversion and settlement partners. A good assessment follows that chain of obligations instead of assuming a one-dollar target eliminates counterparty risk.

For additional perspective, it is worth reading our existing reporting on Binance’s earlier phased withdrawal restart and the September-end Tether reserve disclosure. They explain related market structure and should not be mistaken for evidence that every new proposal is already live.

What the announcement does not prove

Tether’s announcement gives the company’s account of its involvement; it does not independently establish the ultimate ownership or recoverability of every frozen token. Some illicit proceeds may have moved through assets or networks outside the issuer’s control. And a publicly reported freeze total cannot be added to other recovery figures without checking whether they cover the same funds.

Stablecoin adoption depends heavily on ordinary financial services at the edges. Funding accounts, meeting identity rules, accessing banking partners and redeeming balances remain necessary even if a token transfer settles quickly. A project that solves those steps can be useful, but that usefulness cannot be established from headline issuance or a partnership announcement alone.

What to watch next

Watch for validated recoveries, legally authorised unfreezing or transfer procedures and clearer accounting of overlapping industry freeze figures. The longer-term issue is whether issuers can develop fast, reviewable processes that protect innocent users while meeting legitimate law-enforcement demands. A successful freeze is the start of an asset-preservation story, not necessarily its final chapter.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Tuesday, 03/11/2026 | 19:51 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Mohamed Elsergany Brings More Than Eight Years of Experience at Swissquote and PU Prime.
  • Recently, PU Prime, APC Prime and Match-Prime Liquidity Have Also Made Senior MENA Appointments.

Mohamed Elsergany has joined Exclusive Markets as Chief Executive Officer of MENA, according to a LinkedIn post shared by the executive.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Elsergany moves to the broker after spending four years at PU Prime, where he held two senior management positions overseeing the MENA region.

Elsergany's Career Spans Swissquote and PU Prime

He most recently served as CEO of MENA at PU Prime for two years and eight months. Before that, he spent one year and four months as the broker's Managing Director for MENA.

Earlier in his career, Elsergany worked at Swissquote as a Business Development Manager, spending four years and one month at the company.

Brokers Continue Hiring Across the MENA Region

His appointment comes as brokers continue to recruit regional executives and expand their presence in the Middle East. In February, PU Prime obtained a Category 5 licence in Dubai, joining several CFD brokers that have established a presence in the UAE.

The licence allows firms to promote products offered by offshore entities but does not permit them to hold client assets or execute trades locally.

Other brokers have also made senior appointments in the region. In September, Dubai-based APC Prime appointed Shadi Salloum, formerly MENA Director at XS.com, as its Global CEO. Match-Prime Liquidity hired Kareem Harras as Head of MENA in January to lead its regional expansion.

Meanwhile, ACCM outlined plans to enter the MENA and European markets, while Capital.com appeared to be expanding its local presence through director-level recruitment in Bahrain and Azerbaijan.

Earlier examples of regional expansion include GBE Brokers, which opened a Dubai office and appointed a regional executive in 2022, and Traze, which hired Wassim Anastasiou as its MENA Regional Director in November 2025.

His appointment comes as brokers continue to recruit regional executives and expand their presence in the Middle East. In February, PU Prime obtained a Category 5 licence in Dubai, joining several CFD brokers that have established a presence in the UAE.

The licence allows firms to promote products offered by offshore entities but does not permit them to hold client assets or execute trades locally.

Other brokers have also made senior appointments in the region. In September, Dubai-based APC Prime appointed Shadi Salloum, formerly MENA Director at XS.com, as its Global CEO. Match-Prime Liquidity hired Kareem Harras as Head of MENA in January to lead its regional expansion.

Meanwhile, ACCM outlined plans to enter the MENA and European markets, while Capital.com appeared to be expanding its local presence through director-level recruitment in Bahrain and Azerbaijan.

Earlier examples of regional expansion include GBE Brokers, which opened a Dubai office and appointed a regional executive in 2022, and Traze, which hired Wassim Anastasiou as its MENA Regional Director in November 2025.

title: US midterms: Prediction markets favor Democrats in key crypto races
summary: Kalshi and Polymarket price a 75% chance of a Democratic sweep, days after markets misjudged Brazil’s runoff.
content:
Update (Nov. 3 at 10:32 p.m. UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from Talos.

As Americans across the country head to the polls for the US midterm elections Tuesday, prediction market traders have spent months wagering on the outcome. According to an analysis by The Washington Post, nearly $1.9 billion in election-related contracts had traded on Kalshi and Polymarket as of Monday, marking record trading activity for a midterm election cycle.

Markets on both platforms favor Democrats winning control of Congress, with a Democratic sweep priced at 75% on Kalshi and 75.5% on Polymarket as of 4:30 pm UTC. Kalshi traders gave Democrats a 93% chance of taking the House and a 75% chance of winning the Senate, while Polymarket priced those outcomes at 94.5% and 75.5%, respectively.

The vote comes nine days after prediction markets failed to anticipate the outcome of Brazil’s presidential election, with Flávio Bolsonaro favored at roughly 80% the day before incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the runoff. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour reportedly cautioned that “a 5% probability doesn’t mean it won’t happen,” according to CNBC.

For the crypto industry, a shift in congressional control could reshape the prospects for long-awaited regulatory clarity.

PAC spending may fall short in Ohio

A key race for crypto has centered on the Senate seat in Ohio, where Defend American Jobs, part of the Fairshake super PAC network, allocated 54% of its total expenses. According to the official website, $36.9 million was spent on supporting Senator Jon Husted and $19.7 million opposing the staunch crypto critic, Democrat Sherrod Brown. Fairshake spent $40 million to help unseat Brown in 2024.

However, the flood of spending may be to no avail, with traders expecting a win for Brown. The Kalshi market for the race predicted a 72% chance for a Brown win and 72.5% on Polymarket, both in line with a final New York Times/Siena poll that had him ahead 49% to 44%. 

A Brown victory could complicate the crypto industry’s legislative agenda, particularly if Democrats regain control of the Senate. Analysts have identified him as a potential chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, although the leadership position remains uncertain.

Related: From Uptober to Hacktober: Are Bitcoin’s seasonal patterns becoming obsolete?

A pro-crypto shift in Maine

In Maine, however, a Democratic win predicted by traders could help the crypto industry expand its influence in Washington. Republican Senator Susan Collins was one of four Republicans who voted against advancing the CLARITY Act in September, stalling the bill in the Senate. 

Kalshi gives Democrat Troy Jackson a 71% chance of unseating her, while Polymarket puts his chances at 71.5%, broadly in line with New York Times polls conducted in October that had Jackson ahead by two percentage points. Advocacy group Stand with Crypto rates Jackson as strongly supportive of crypto, potentially giving the industry another ally in the Senate should he win.

Predicting the coin flips 

Although many prediction markets are broadly in line with polling results, traders have made clearer calls in three states where polls show close races.

In Alaska, Kalshi gives Democrat Mary Peltola a 71% chance of defeating Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, even though the final New York Times/Siena poll had her ahead by just two percentage points, 48% to 46%. Both candidates have expressed strong support for crypto, according to Stand With Crypto.

In South Carolina, where the candidates were tied at 48% in the New York Times/Siena poll, Kalshi gives Republican Senator Darline Graham, a crypto supporter, a 71% chance of defeating Democrat Annie Andrews.

Iowa remains a toss-up on both platforms, with Democrat Josh Turek overtaking Republican Representative Ashley Hinson on Polymarket at 52%, after months of Hinson being favored to win.

In other key races, prediction markets are broadly in line with the polls. In Michigan, Kalshi gives Democrat Abdul El-Sayed a 79% chance of defeating Republican Mike Rogers. Kalshi also gives Democrat James Talarico a 71% chance of defeating Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, while the final New York Times/Siena poll had Talarico ahead 50% to 43%. A Paxton loss would be a setback for the Digital Freedom Fund, a super PAC backed by Gemini’s co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss that spent more than $81,000 supporting his campaign. However, Talarico has also expressed support for the crypto industry.

Related: What’s at stake for crypto as the US votes in the 2026 midterms?

Thin liquidity, quick repricing

Despite the markets leaning towards a Democrat win in both the House and Senate, researchers from Talos have pointed to thin liquidity behind the contracts. According to Talos’ head of research, Kelly Ye, as of 11:30 am ET, just $300,000 of selling would have pushed Kalshi’s Democrats-win-Senate contract down ten points.

The median trade on the markets came in at around $10, with a few large-ticket trades making up the majority of the liquidity behind the contracts.

“As midterm results come in tonight, prediction markets will reprice quickly, but those prices are only as good as the liquidity behind them,” she said in a statement sent to Cointelegraph.

“Whatever happens tonight, one result won’t tell you whether these markets are accurate. Across many settled contracts, outcomes have broadly tracked prices.”

What traders expect after a sweep

Markets are also starting to look beyond today’s vote to the political and economic landscape following a potential Democratic sweep of Congress. Polymarket’s conditional markets suggest traders are pricing in a higher risk of recession under Democratic control of both chambers, with the implied probability of a US recession by the end of 2027 at 35% if Democrats sweep and 19% if they do not, as of 4:50 pm UTC.

Tuesday, 03/11/2026 | 18:36 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • A months-long cyberattack used compromised engineers and internal AI tools to breach Binance wallets.
  • Hackers posed as company executives before using stolen credentials to access Binance's hot wallets.

Binance has disclosed further details of a $6.3 billion cyberattack that involved fake job interviews, malicious software and an internal artificial intelligence tool. The exchange said the campaign began in June and ended with the theft of digital assets in October.

London's trading industry is coming home!

According to an incident report published today (Tuesday), attackers initially compromised an engineer's computer through a tampered version of Homebrew, a software package manager. The employee had downloaded it after clicking an online advertisement while searching for an AI coding tool.

Hackers Exploited Employee Devices and Internal AI

Binance detected the suspicious activity, replaced the employee's device and changed the affected credentials. However, the attackers had already gathered information about the engineer and other members of the wallet development team.

In September, the hackers approached another engineer through a job-hunting platform. They posed as representatives of a fictitious company and arranged interviews with individuals claiming to be its executives. During the process, the engineer received a coding assignment containing malicious software.

The compromised devices provided further access to Binance's internal systems. On October 20, the attackers used an internal AI tool and information from the compromised computers to access the systems of two wallet developers.

Binance Hot Wallets Drained Across Multiple Blockchains

The attack escalated on October 29, when the hackers used stolen credentials to deploy a container and run a malicious script. They exploited Ethereum 's mechanism to obtain execution permissions over a Binance hot wallet, allowing them to initiate unauthorised transactions.

The attackers first moved approximately 233 million XRP from five internet-connected wallets. They then targeted wallets across multiple blockchains, stealing approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets.

FBI Attributes Attack to North Korea

The FBI attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea. The group has previously been associated with major cryptocurrency thefts, including the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.

North Korea denied involvement. Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, described the FBI's attribution as a political provocation.

Binance said it detected and blocked 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyberattacks in 2026. Many involved fraudulent recruitment approaches and malicious software.

title: Tether Holds 150,000 Bitcoin CEO Says, 50,000 More Than Its Reserve Report Shows
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Tether Holds 150,000 Bitcoin CEO Says, 50,000 More Than Its Reserve Report Shows
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in Lugano that the company holds about 150,000 bitcoin worth $11.5 billion. 
This post Tether Holds 150,000 Bitcoin CEO Says, 50,000 More Than Its Reserve Report Shows fir...
content:
Tether holds about 150,000 bitcoin, worth some $11.5 billion at current prices, CEO Paolo Ardoino said, a figure that exceeds the holdings implied by the company’s latest reserve attestation by roughly 50,000 coins.

“We have give or take 150,000 bitcoin ourselves. It’s not much, but it’s honest work,” Ardoino said during his keynote at the Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, Switzerland, the city where Tether has run a bitcoin and stablecoin adoption program since 2022.

At that size the stack would rank Tether among the largest corporate holders of bitcoin, behind Strategy’s 848,517 BTC (as of Q3) and ahead of most public miners and treasury companies. 

Ardoino did not say where the additional coins sit, when they were bought or whether they belong to the stablecoin issuer or to Tether Investments, the arm that holds the group’s venture and equity positions. The remark does not indicate a new 50,000 BTC purchase.

Tether International’s third-quarter reserve report, published Oct. 30 with an attestation from BDO, lists $8.37 billion in bitcoin valued at $83,621.23 per coin as of Sept. 30. That implies about 100,060 BTC, up around 1,130 from the roughly 98,930 held at the end of June. Most of the quarter’s $2.57 billion rise in the bitcoin line came from price, not purchases.

The gap between the report and Ardoino’s figure has a plausible home. Tether has said the investments it makes from profits are kept apart from the reserves backing USDT, so coins held by Tether Investments would not appear in the attestation. 

Tether’s bitcoin exposure extends past its own wallets. It took full control of Twenty One Capital in May after buying out SoftBank, backs Adecoagro’s mining in Brazil, and runs mining and energy ventures in Latin America. Whether any of those positions sit inside the 150,000 figure is unclear.

Tether’s buffer built on bitcoin and gold

The disclosure lands as Tether’s balance sheet grows more dependent on the two assets. The Q3 report shows $191.45 billion in reserve assets against $183.50 billion in liabilities, an excess of $7.95 billion, up from $4.11 billion in June when the cushion had halved. 

Bitcoin at $8.37 billion and gold at about $19.1 billion together exceed that buffer several times over, so a sharp drop in either would eat into it. Treasury bills remain the bulk of reserves at about $132.4 billion.

Tether earned about $1.5 billion in the quarter and $4.5 billion in the first nine months. In August it completed its first independent audit with KPMG, ending years of reliance on attestations alone. Ardoino said at the forum that USDT has more than 730 million users and is adding about 30 million wallets a quarter.

title: TD Cowen: Democratic Congress Would Sink CLARITY Act for Two Years
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

TD Cowen: Democratic Congress Would Sink CLARITY Act for Two Years
TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg says a Democratic sweep of Congress would kill the CLARITY Act for two years, hand Elizabeth Warren the Banking Committee and let Democrats block Trump’s picks for the SEC and CFTC.
This pos...
content:
A Democratic sweep of Congress would end the CLARITY Act’s chances for the next two years and sour the political climate for crypto, TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg wrote to Bitcoin Magazine and clients in an election-day note.

Seiberg wrote that TD Cowen agrees with polls and prediction markets that Democrats are likely to take both chambers, with the caveat that polls taken a month out, which were more mixed, tend to beat those taken on the eve of a vote. 

His conclusion for crypto is blunt: “Democrats will likely investigate Trump including his crypto entanglements. We see this as souring the political environment for crypto, which is why we do not expect the Clarity Act to pass over the next two years.”

The market structure bill passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. If it does not pass before the new Congress convenes on Jan. 3, it dies and must be reintroduced. 

Seiberg added that crypto’s influence may shrink further in Congress if Sherrod Brown wins his Ohio Senate race, a contest the industry spent to lose.

In Congress, the Senate is the lever

The note treats Senate control as the bigger prize. A Democratic majority could block Trump’s nominees and use that power to force him to fill Democratic seats on the FDIC, SEC and CFTC, the three agencies at the center of crypto policy. 

It could pressure the White House to drop its effort to remove Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve board. Trump could answer with acting chiefs, Seiberg wrote, but that risks handing authority to career staff, an outcome “Team Trump” does not want.

Senate control would elevate Sen. Elizabeth Warren to chair the Banking Committee. Seiberg sees room for populist bills such as interest rate caps, limits on bank buybacks and a government credit score, and he thinks Warren and Trump could find common ground on some of them.

Rep. Maxine Waters would take House Financial Services, with a focus on housing and tighter scrutiny of the FHFA.

“That means a focus on housing though we are dubious that she will find GOP support for down payment help and public housing renovations. FHFA scrutiny will increase,” the note read.

For banks, the note says the election changes little: regulators will keep easing capital, liquidity and tiering rules whichever party wins. Divided government does raise the odds of a shutdown or a debt-ceiling standoff, since Trump is expected to reject spending conditions Democrats attach.

Bitcoin on election day

Bitcoin traded near $77,500 Tuesday afternoon eastern time, up from a dip to $76,300 in the morning and about $2,000 below where it opened the month. The price has absorbed a record $6.34 billion Binance hack, two days of spot ETF outflows and a Fed that is leaning toward a December hike. 

Prediction markets on Kalshi give Democrats a 94% chance at the House and 74% at the Senate, so much of Seiberg’s scenario is in the price.

What is not priced is the lame-duck session. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, a CLARITY negotiator, has said the bill could pass before January even if a Democratic Congress would not make it a priority after. That said, if it fails during that window, she doubts a Democratic-controlled Congress will make it a priority in the future.

According to various reports, crypto groups have spent more than $200 million on the cycle to avoid the outcome Seiberg now expects. The CFTC, for its part, moved without Congress on Tuesday, clearing equity perpetual futures for U.S. exchanges. If the Senate and Congress flips, that agency-by-agency approach, and who sits on those agencies, becomes the whole game.

title: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen
summary: Markus Thielen sees Bitcoin reaching $90,000 by year-end, questions institutional ETF demand and says Ethereum must do more for holders.
content:
Bitcoin’s days of consecutive double-digit price surges are over as Wall Street traders and profit-taking whales reshape the market, according to 10x Research founder Markus Thielen.

Institutional traders selling call options after rallies have made Bitcoin’s violent price explosions of earlier years less common, Thielen says in the latest episode of Cointelegraph’s Trade Secrets.

Thielen is also the author of Crypto Titans, a history of the industry. Writing the book led him to notice how each cycle brought different people pitching crypto to investors.

“Every cycle had actually different promoters, and different promoters bring in different investors,” he says.

This time, the promoters come from Wall Street, where investors trade on economic data and Federal Reserve decisions. Thielen says he expects Bitcoin will rise quickly on news, then spend time crab walking across the chart before the next big macro event.

Who’s really buying Bitcoin?

Thielen estimates that market makers account for up to half of the $60 billion in net spot Bitcoin ETF inflows he analyzed. Those firms hold ETF shares as a way to hedge their options trades, so the positions do not necessarily represent a bet that Bitcoin’s price will rise.

“So in the end it was not outright buying,” he says.

His estimate draws on a review of Form 13F filings, which disclose certain securities holdings of investment managers.

Thielen says the first wave of funds into the ETFs also included retail investors buying through institutions and corporate vehicles. Some paid substantial premiums to the value of the underlying crypto holdings.

“I would still think the institutions could come. I would still think that some of the sovereign wealth funds could come,” Thielen says.

Bitcoin could reach $90,000 by year-end

Thielen still sees Bitcoin reaching $90,000 by year-end. He says a drop into the mid-to-high $70,000s could come first.

Bitcoin has already been trading in that range, falling to about $76,100 on Friday following Binance’s $6.3 billion hack. BTC finished October down 7.3%, according to Coinglass.

Thielen compares the recovery in prices over recent months with early 2023, when Bitcoin rose from around $20,000 to $30,000. He says the doubts surrounding this year’s rebound are familiar as investors scan for the next price drop and entry point.

“I think everybody sort of missed it. So everybody wants to buy again.”

BTC’s return to $90,000 may rest partly on how much further the Fed raises borrowing rates. The central bank increased its benchmark rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September, to a target range of 3.75%–4%.

It held rates steady last Wednesday in a split vote, with two officials voting for another quarter-point increase. The Fed’s statement said inflation was still elevated, leaving open the possibility of further increases.

Thielen expects another hike by December, followed by a more cautious approach to further increases that could help Bitcoin rally toward year-end.

Ethereum needs to show holders the money

Thielen expects Bitcoin to outperform Ether, saying too much of the value from Ethereum activity goes to layer-2 networks.

“I look at it more as like a valuable utility, but nobody wants to pay for it.”

Making those networks cheaper to use has been a deliberate part of Ethereum’s development. But cheaper transactions may muddy the investment pitch for ETH. 

Ethereum burns base fees paid by users, removing those coins from circulation. Its supply shrinks when the amount burned exceeds new ETH issued to validators. Lower fees can mean less ETH is destroyed.

ETH supply grows when issuance exceeds the amount burned. Source: ultrasound.money

Thielen, who says he has been bearish on Ether for more than a year, compares Ethereum with a highway. 

“Everybody wants the highway to be empty so you can go fast, and the roads need to be super, super clean and fixed and everything, but nobody wants to pay for it,” he says.

He singles out Hyperliquid as an example of how trading activity can fund token purchases. The decentralized perpetuals exchange’s assistance fund converts trading fees into HYPE, which is then burned.

For Ethereum, he wants a stronger connection between the network’s use and the financial benefit to holders.

title: Binance Says $6.34 Billion Hack Began With Fake Job Interview
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Says $6.34 Billion Hack Began With Fake Job Interview 
Binance’s incident report says the $6.34 billion Oct. 29 theft was a five-month campaign that began with a fake job interview and a poisoned developer tool.
This post Binance Says $6.34 Billion Hack Began With Fake Job ...
content:
The $6.34 billion theft from Binance began with a fake job interview and ran for five months before a single coin moved, the exchange said Tuesday in its first public account of the Oct. 29 attack.

Another initial incident report from Binance, released alongside a media briefing by co-CEO Richard Teng and chief security officer Jimmy Su, describes a campaign that combined a poisoned software download, a staged recruitment process, malware that evaded endpoint detection and an internal AI tool the attackers turned against the company’s own wallet engineers. 

Binance said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion of the stolen assets and replenished 98% of affected tokens from its own funds, with the balance being bought on the open market.

“This wasn’t one mistake or one breach — it was a months-long campaign,” Teng wrote on X. “We’re publishing the full report because the lessons go far beyond Binance.”

The FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea. Binance’s report cites that finding but stops short of its own attribution. Pyongyang rejected the claim Monday, with Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, calling it a “grave political provocation” through state media.

The Binance hack had five months of preparation

According to Binance, the first foothold for this hack came in June. A wallet DevOps engineer searched for a popular AI coding tool and downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer. 

Binance’s security team caught the anomaly, replaced the device and rotated credentials, but the episode exposed the engineer’s role and the names of colleagues on the wallet infrastructure team.

In September, a second engineer was approached on a legitimate job platform by someone posing as a project director. A video interview with a purported HR representative followed, with the interviewer sharing a personal social media account to build trust. A second interview with a supposed CEO ended with an “assignment”: a code repository the engineer was told to install on his work machine. 

The repository replaced a legitimate pyenv component with a malicious version and opened a channel to an attacker-controlled server. Binance said the zero-day malware was not flagged by its endpoint tools at the time.

On Oct. 20, the attackers used that machine and an internal AI tool to reach two more wallet engineers, one of whom held a container deployment token. On Oct. 29, between 17:15 and 19:56 UTC, they logged into a third engineer’s computer, deployed a container with the stolen credentials and launched the drain. Binance said it blocked 57 other suspected North Korea-linked attempts this year using similar lures.

Four hours to contain

The money left fast. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. Wallets on Solana and Optimism followed with about 970,500 SOL and 44.2 million OP. A Binance hot wallet then sent 18,270 BTC. 

The attacker used the compromised signing service to invoke Ethereum’s EIP-7702, which lets an account delegate execution rights to a smart contract without exposing its key, and gave an attacker-controlled contract partial control of a Binance hot wallet.

Suspending withdrawals did not stop that last channel. The attackers had submitted 50 signing transactions to establish on-chain delegations that operated outside Binance’s withdrawal infrastructure. Because the wallet used multi-party computation, no single key existed to revoke them, and the team had to build a procedure on the spot. The final unauthorized transfer, 2,961.9 ETH, settled at 23:56 UTC. 

Binance cleared the delegation at 00:10 UTC on Oct. 30.

The report acknowledges the gap. “These challenges extended the time required to fully contain the unauthorized asset movements,” it says, adding that the company is reviewing its signing policy coverage and hot wallet controls.

Customers withdrew $10.97 billion in the 46 hours after withdrawals reopened Sunday, with net outflows of $5.28 billion, according todata Teng shared Tuesday. By 03:00 UTC hourly deposits exceeded withdrawals, a shift Teng called a sign of stabilization. Binance reopened withdrawals for dozens more assets across nine networks on Tuesday.

The breach has become a talking point in Washington. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said the hack “proves our exact point” about the need for a federal registration path for offshore exchanges, and on Tuesday the agency cleared equity perpetual futures for U.S.-regulated venues, extending the onshoring push it began with Kalshi’s bitcoin perp in May.

Binance said it has rebuilt the wallet system and the internal AI tool in new environments, replaced affected devices, revoked the engineers’ credentials and expanded behavioral anomaly detection. 

It is commissioning an independent review, raising spending on endpoint and developer-environment security and planning a research fund on AI security with outside firms. Some technical details, the report says, will stay private. 

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: CFTC Allows Perpetual Futures to Expand from Bitcoin to Individual Stocks
summary:
The US Commodity
Futures Trading Commission has allowed perpetual futures contracts linked to
individual stocks to trade on CFTC-registered exchanges for the first time.
London's trading industry is coming home!
Chairman Michael S.
Selig announced the development today (Tuesday), saying it extends t...
content:
2026-11-03T18:06:21.319+02:00

Tuesday, 03/11/2026 | 16:06 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Equity Perps fall under a joint regulatory framework involving the CFTC and SEC.
  • The CFTC aims to bring perpetual derivatives into US markets under existing regulatory safeguards.

The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission has allowed perpetual futures contracts linked to individual stocks to trade on CFTC-registered exchanges for the first time.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the development today (Tuesday), saying it extends the availability of perpetual futures in the US beyond digital assets and into traditional securities.

The contracts, known as Equity Perps, were deemed approved under Commission Regulation as security futures products. They are subject to the Commodity Exchange Act, US federal securities laws and the regulatory frameworks of both the CFTC and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

CFTC Expands Perpetual Futures Framework

The move follows the CFTC's approval earlier this year of the first Bitcoin perpetual futures contract on a CFTC -regulated exchange.

In his inaugural remarks, Selig directed the agency to use its existing powers to bring perpetual derivatives into US markets, subject to appropriate safeguards.

He said the latest approval would allow US market participants to use perpetual futures for risk management and price discovery within the country's regulatory framework. He also said the move could reduce reliance on offshore venues.

@ChairmanSelig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures: https://t.co/aZAEa77sE7

— CFTC (@CFTC) November 3, 2026

CFTC and SEC Joint Regulatory Framework

The approval builds on the CFMA, which established a framework for the joint regulation of security futures products by the CFTC and SEC.

Earlier this year, the two agencies also signed a memorandum of understanding to improve coordination and cooperation.

Selig said the framework addresses regulatory uncertainty that had left products such as security futures and equity perpetual futures in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins described as a regulatory "no man's land".

title: Binance Sees Deposits Overtake Withdrawals as It Covers 95% of Stolen Assets
summary: Binance reported that hourly deposits overtook withdrawals by 03:00 UTC on November 3, marking a shift in exchange flows as its recovery from a $6.3 billion security breach continues.
content:
Skip to content

Binance reported that hourly deposits overtook withdrawals by 03:00 UTC on November 3, marking a shift in exchange flows as its recovery from a $6.3 billion security breach continues.

The update comes as the exchange expands withdrawal access across multiple blockchain networks and reports replenishing approximately 95% of the assets affected by the October 29 incident.

Binance Deposits Overtake Withdrawals as Exchange Flows Stabilize

Binance announced on November 3 that deposits had started exceeding withdrawals on an hourly basis, pointing to improving activity following several days of heavy outflows. The exchange attributed the change to stabilizing transaction flows as users gradually resumed normal activity.

In its update, the exchange stated, “By 03:00 UTC, we are seeing hourly deposits exceed withdrawals, reflecting improving user activity and stabilizing flows.”

A 60-minute chart tracking Binance deposits, withdrawals, and net flows from November 1–3 shows that initial heavy outflows have gradually moderated. Source: Binance/X

The exchange also published a 60-minute interval chart covering deposits, withdrawals, and net flows between November 1 and November 3. The figures showed approximately $10.97 billion in withdrawals against $5.695 billion in deposits, resulting in a cumulative net outflow of around $5.276 billion during the 46-hour period.

Withdrawal activity was particularly intense shortly after the exchange began restoring services on November 1. The largest hourly outflow reached approximately $1.243 billion during the 08:00 UTC interval that day. Subsequent readings showed lower withdrawal volumes, while deposits gradually increased.

By the final hourly interval in the chart, deposits had reached approximately $193 million, compared with $183 million in withdrawals, producing a net inflow of around $10 million.

Although the latest reading marked a positive change, the cumulative figures showed that more funds had left Binance than entered during the broader measurement period. The hourly reversal therefore represents an early indication of stabilizing activity rather than a complete recovery in customer flows.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng also addressed the exchange’s financial position during Hong Kong Fintech Week on November 3. He said withdrawal activity had initially increased following the incident but had subsequently “pretty much normalised.”

Teng added that the exchange remained in a position to absorb the financial impact of the security breach. Reuters reported that Binance had recorded approximately $4.72 billion in net customer withdrawals by Monday, representing around 3% of its platform assets.

Binance Expands Crypto Withdrawal Access Across Networks

Alongside the improving deposit figures, Binance has continued restoring withdrawal services through a phased process designed to complete security checks before reopening individual assets and networks.

In its November 3 recovery update, the exchange announced another round of withdrawal restoration beginning at 04:00 UTC. The expansion covers dozens of cryptocurrencies across BNB Smart Chain, Ethereum, Solana, XRP Ledger, Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron, and Base.

Binance has expanded withdrawal access to dozens of additional assets across Ethereum and Solana, including major tokens and memecoins, following its initial rollout. Source: Binance/X

The restored asset list includes Shiba Inu (SHIB), Chainlink (LINK), Pendle (PENDLE), dogwifhat (WIF), and Bonk (BONK), among other tokens. Additional assets include Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Cardano (ADA), Litecoin (LTC), Polkadot (DOT), and several stablecoins.

The latest phase follows the initial reopening on November 1, when Binance restored selected withdrawals for assets including BTC, ETH, USDT, USDC, BNB, SOL, XRP, and ZEC across supported networks.

However, the exchange clarified that the newly listed assets would not all become available simultaneously. Each network and asset combination must pass the required security and operational readiness checks before withdrawals resume.

Binance said it was prioritizing assets based on user demand over the preceding week. Deposits have remained operational throughout the withdrawal restrictions, allowing customers to continue transferring supported assets into their accounts.

The exchange also introduced an additional wallet security measure. On November 1, the exchange updated its Proof of Reserves address list with newly generated wallet addresses and confirmed that future withdrawals would be processed through these addresses.

Binance Replenishes 95% of Assets Affected by $6.3B Hack

The withdrawal restoration follows Binance’s efforts to replace the approximately $6.3 billion in token assets stolen during the October 29 security breach.

Binance confirmed in its November 1 recovery update that it had replenished approximately 95% of the impacted amount, increasing from the previously reported 90%. The exchange attributed the recovery to its own financial resources, including the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate treasury funds.

The remaining 5% consists of less-liquid tokens outside the ten largest affected asset categories. Binance said these assets require additional time to acquire in sufficient quantities and that it continues working with industry partners and over-the-counter (OTC) providers to complete the purchases.

The exchange has also increased its Proof of Reserves disclosures to provide users with additional verification of their account backing.

On November 2, Binance announced that it had completed the zero-knowledge (ZK) proof for its October 31 Proof of Reserves snapshot. Users holding BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC can independently verify that their balances are backed by reserves at a minimum 1:1 ratio.

The verification process allows users to check the backing of their balances without requiring Binance to disclose sensitive information about individual accounts. The exchange also planned another reserve snapshot for November 4, covering additional tokens, with the subsequent ZK proof expected to take approximately 40 to 50 hours to generate.

The exchange has maintained that customers will not bear the financial impact of the stolen funds. The company has also committed to publishing a detailed post-incident report after its investigation is complete.

FBI Attributes Binance Hack to North Korea-Linked Actors

The October 29 security incident remains the central issue behind Binance’s recovery efforts. The exchange initially reported that compromised hot wallets resulted in approximately $6.3 billion in unauthorized withdrawals.

The FBI attributed the October 29 Binance theft to North Korean state-backed hackers operating under the TraderTraitor campaign, identifying it as the largest known crypto heist. Source: FBI via X

Binance’s preliminary investigation pointed to a possible compromise involving a DevOps engineer’s laptop, which may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. The exchange later identified additional points of compromise but said it had found no evidence that wallet private keys were leaked.

On October 31, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the theft to North Korea, identifying the activity as part of the TraderTraitor hacking operation.

The agency reported that the attackers had primarily converted the stolen assets into Ethereum (ETH), potentially preparing them for further laundering through decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms and instant swap services. The FBI also urged cryptocurrency exchanges, blockchain infrastructure providers, and other industry participants to block transactions connected to the identified addresses.

North Korea rejected the US attribution, describing the allegations as unacceptable rhetoric, Reuters reported.

Meanwhile, Binance has continued cooperating with law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence firms to trace the stolen funds and support recovery efforts.

The latest deposit figures and expanded withdrawal access indicate progress in restoring the exchange’s operations. However, the cumulative net outflow, outstanding asset replenishment, and ongoing security investigation show that Binance’s recovery process remains incomplete.

title: Coinbase Launches AI Agent Sign-Ups for Crypto Trading With Built-In Safety Limits
summary:
Key Takeaways: Coinbase has created a special page for AI agents to sign up. Actively search and trade crypto under AI tools under user-set limits. Every agent trades within Coinbase,
The post Coinbase Launches AI Agent Sign-Ups for Crypto Trading With Built-In Safety Limits appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Coinbase has created a special page for AI agents to sign up.
  • Actively search and trade crypto under AI tools under user-set limits.
  • Every agent trades within Coinbase, with separate portfolios and security measures.

Growing its platform more directly towards AI-driven trading, Coinbase has launched a new web page aimed at specifically registering software agents. CEO Brian Armstrong said the company wants Coinbase to become the “most AI-enabled financial account,” while the new Agents product lets users connect existing AI tools to their Coinbase accounts.

We added a new sign up page for Agents.

We’re building Coinbase to be the most AI-enabled financial account.

Give it a try: https://t.co/Vx3wBHQ0DT https://t.co/ObNGeBdX9T

— Brian Armstrong (@brian_armstrong) November 2, 2026

Read More: Coinbase Unveils AiFi After $100M in x402 Transactions, Targeting AI Agent Payments

  • Coinbase Opens Dedicated Access for AI Agents
  • Crypto Trading Moves Into Plain-Language Commands
    • Coinbase Adds Limits Around Automated Trading
    • USDC Payments Give Agents Access to Premium Data

Coinbase Opens Dedicated Access for AI Agents

The Coinbase for Agents page enables users to integrate AI assistants that support the agency and grant their access to the agency’s Coinbase accounts. The list of compatible tools means that tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Perplexity, Cursor, Hermes and Muse are all supported for use with Coinbase. Any agent that supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) can connect, but Coinbase also provides a command-line tool to connect for non-MCP agents.

After the connection, an agent can browse markets, examine one to in several situations make trades according to instructions from the account owner. Coinbase emphasises that the AI isn’t meant for Coinbase to make investment decisions for them. Rather, it follows instructions and permissions set by the user.

Read More: Coinbase Lists $2.6B RLUSD Across XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base

Crypto Trading Moves Into Plain-Language Commands

The major difference is that one can order trades without having to create a traditional trading bot in a programmatic language.

For instance, Coinbase provides examples like telling an agent to reprice a portfolio or make a recurring purchase of Bitcoin. More conditional instructions also are supported on the board, with reference to the market indicators.

Coinbase Adds Limits Around Automated Trading

Coinbase has put in place several controls on access by agents. Users can seek approval prior to trades, create a separate portfolio for their agent and can pull disconnection anytime. Coinbase also states effective 8 a.m. ET on Tuesday, agents were not allowed to transfer money out of exchanges.

All agents are subject to a limit imposed by Coinbase, thus minimizing the access of automated software to the accounts. The firm also notes that AI agents may make mistakes and the user is still in charge of agent actions and their trading choices.

USDC Payments Give Agents Access to Premium Data

AI agents are being paired with paid market data by Coinbase as well, with x402, an open payments standard for software agents.

Agent users in the US are able to access top-notch research and market data for purchase, without subscription or API key. Coinbase has set those limits at $5 per transaction and $50 a day at this point.

Unlike other platforms, there is no separate fee for Coinbase for agents, and trades by agents can be done with the same fees as the other Coinbase trades.
