title: Tradeview Markets CEO on EDGE, AI Execution, and Why Trading Conditions Matter More Than Bonuses
summary:
Tradeview Markets' strategy focuses on proprietary execution technology, with founder and CEO Timothy Furey emphasising that better order routing and liquidity access matter more to serious traders than promotional incentives.
Speaking with Finance Magnates CEO Neophytos Papageorgiou at iFX EXPO Asi...
content:
Tradeview Markets' strategy focuses on proprietary execution technology, with founder and CEO Timothy Furey emphasising that better order routing and liquidity access matter more to serious traders than promotional incentives.

Speaking with Finance Magnates CEO Neophytos Papageorgiou at iFX EXPO Asia 2026 in Hong Kong, Furey discussed the development of EDGE, Tradeview's new execution engine, the role of artificial intelligence in liquidity management, and the company's expansion into cryptocurrency trading.

From the Trading Floor to Tradeview's EDGE

Furey's approach to trading technology dates back to his career on the Chicago Board of Trade in the late 1990s, when open-outcry trading and hand signals were still part of daily market activity.

For floor traders, finding an "edge" meant identifying opportunities where they had an advantage in entering and exiting positions.

As electronic trading replaced traditional trading floors, Furey moved into screen-based trading and later worked for a hedge fund. The search for better execution remained central to his approach.

That experience eventually influenced the development of EDGE Instant Liquidity Connector, Tradeview's proprietary execution engine, which Furey said took more than two years to build, alongside earlier technology development.

Rather than relying entirely on third-party infrastructure, Tradeview chose to develop its own execution technology to address problems Furey had encountered throughout his trading career.

"It's like a race car, right? A race car looks great on the outside, but what makes it go is the engine inside."

According to Furey, the company invested millions in developing and testing EDGE before bringing it into live operation.

How EDGE Uses AI to Improve Liquidity Routing and Trade Execution

One of the central themes of the interview was the difference between the trading platform visible to clients and the execution infrastructure operating behind it.

While traders using MetaTrader 4 or MetaTrader 5 can place orders through familiar interfaces, the quality of execution depends partly on how those orders are routed and filled.

Furey explained that EDGE uses a smart order-routing system designed to identify suitable liquidity across approximately 20 providers.

"We have about 20 liquidity providers and it looks for the best bid, best offer, right?"

The system also uses AI-assisted technology to anticipate incoming orders and determine where they are more likely to receive execution without unnecessary slippage.

Slippage occurs when an order is executed at a different price from the one requested. It can become particularly relevant when trading larger positions or during periods of heightened market volatility.

According to Furey, conventional bridge technology may route an order to the liquidity provider displaying the best available price, but that does not necessarily guarantee execution at that price.

EDGE instead aims to assess the likelihood of a successful fill when selecting where to route an order. The distinction matters because the best quoted price is not always the best executable price. Available liquidity, order size and market conditions can all affect the final execution outcome.

Tradeview says its technology is designed to improve this process through intelligent routing and liquidity aggregation.

Why Tradeview is Prioritising Execution Quality Over Trading Bonuses

Beyond technology, Furey questioned the retail brokerage industry's reliance on deposit bonuses and other promotional incentives to attract clients.

He argued that competition for traders often centres on short-term offers rather than the trading conditions clients experience after opening an account.

For Tradeview, the objective is to attract traders who place greater importance on order execution, pricing and access to liquidity.

"We want long-term clients."

Furey's argument is that traders who choose a broker primarily because of promotional incentives may leave when another provider offers a more attractive deal.

By contrast, he believes execution performance provides a stronger basis for maintaining long-term relationships.

Why Asia Remains a Competitive Market for Tradeview

Speaking from Hong Kong, Furey acknowledged that Tradeview has a smaller presence in Asia than in some of its other markets.

The company is using industry events and direct meetings to establish relationships and introduce its execution technology to potential partners.

Furey identified competition and traders' ability to distinguish between trading offers as challenges in the region.

Rather than relying solely on product demonstrations, he said Tradeview has allowed selected business contacts to test EDGE using accounts funded by him.

The initiative reflects his preference for demonstrating execution capabilities through actual trading rather than relying entirely on promotional claims.

Tradeview's Cryptocurrency Expansion Through YimmiT

The discussion also covered Furey's entry into the cryptocurrency exchange market through YimmiT.

Despite his extensive background in traditional financial markets, Furey said he had previously avoided entering the crypto sector because of concerns about hacking and operational security.

He explained that Tradeview's experience in cybersecurity had increased his confidence in approaching the market.

The company has built a cryptocurrency exchange that draws on its experience in trading infrastructure and order-routing technology.

According to Furey, the smart order-routing engine developed for EDGE has also been incorporated into the cryptocurrency exchange.

The move reflects Tradeview's broader emphasis on developing proprietary systems rather than depending exclusively on external technology providers.

What Comes Next for EDGE and Tradeview Markets?

Furey also discussed the mindset behind his approach to business, recalling advice from his former American football coach that competition rewards those who remain motivated.

He attributed much of his drive to frustration with longstanding problems in the trading industry, particularly issues affecting execution and traders' access to favourable market conditions.

Looking ahead, Furey expressed confidence that EDGE could play a significant role in Tradeview's development over the next 12 months.

title: CFTC Opens U.S. Stock Market to Equity Perpetual Futures
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

CFTC Opens U.S. Stock Market to Equity Perpetual Futures
The CFTC has cleared perpetual futures on individual stocks to trade on dual-registered U.S. exchanges for the first time. 
This post CFTC Opens U.S. Stock Market to Equity Perpetual Futures first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine...
content:
Perpetual futures on individual stocks can begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges for the first time, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Tuesday, extending a product that was confined to offshore crypto venues a year ago into the equity market.

In a statement, CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said the contracts, which he called “Equity Perps,” were deemed approved under Commission Regulation 40.3 as security futures products. 

They may list on exchanges that hold a CFTC designated contract market registration and a notice registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission as a national securities exchange for security futures.

“This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures,” Selig said. He said bringing the products inside the agency’s framework means Americans no longer need to “turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues.”

The contracts fall under the Commodity Exchange Act, federal securities law and the rulebooks of both agencies. The statement names no exchange, lists no contracts and sets no launch date. 

Those details are expected to come from the designated contract markets themselves.

CFTC: From bitcoin perps to stock perps in five months

Perpetual futures have no expiration date. Instead of settling on a fixed day, longs and shorts exchange periodic funding payments that keep the contract price tied to spot. The structure has dominated crypto derivatives for years, with most volume on platforms outside U.S. jurisdiction.

The CFTC approved the first U.S.-listed bitcoin perpetual, Kalshi’s BTCPERP, on May 29, and Kalshi went live with the product soon after. The same day, staff granted no-action relief that lets Coinbase Financial Markets route U.S. clients into offshore perp and options liquidity. Kalshi added gold and silver perpetuals in September. 

In his statement Tuesday, Selig described the equity contracts as an extension of that May decision “beyond digital commodities and into traditional securities.”

The legal basis is older. The Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000 created a joint CFTC-SEC regime for security futures products, and the two agencies signed a memorandum of understanding on March 11 to coordinate rulemaking and enforcement. 

Selig cited both, and repeated SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins’s description of security futures as stranded in a regulatory “no man’s land” for lack of harmonization. The agencies had set out a joint crypto asset taxonomy earlier in the year.

Not everyone accepts the CFTC’s reading. CME Grou  sued the agency in June over the Kalshi approval, arguing that a contract built on exchanged funding payments is a swap under Dodd-Frank, not a future. 

That case is pending. An equity version adds the SEC’s jurisdiction to the mix and may draw a new set of objections from securities-side participants.

The onshoring argument after Binance

The approval lands five days after the largest theft in crypto’s history. On Oct. 29, attackers that TRM Labs and Chainalysis link to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group drained about $6.3 billion from Binance’s hot wallets in roughly 20 minutes. 

Binance reopened withdrawals on Sunday and says it has replenished about 95% of affected assets.

Selig used the breach to press the case he made in Tuesday’s statement. 

“The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States,” he told CNBC on Oct. 30. 

He said the hack “proves our exact point” about the agency’s October proposal, an advance notice of rulemaking that would create a voluntary federal registration path for crypto exchanges with cybersecurity, proof-of-reserves and custody requirements. Selig has said the CFTC cannot make that registration mandatory without Congress.

The equity perp approval works from the same premise. Perpetuals built the offshore derivatives business; moving them onto dual-registered U.S. exchanges puts the margin, clearing and surveillance rules of two federal agencies around them. 

Selig framed it as a choice between regulated access and “being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues.”

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: New Jersey Drops Coinbase Staking Order After Three Years
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

New Jersey Drops Coinbase Staking Order After Three Years
New Jersey’s securities regulator has rescinded its 2023 cease-and-desist order and $5 million penalty against Coinbase’s staking service.
This post New Jersey Drops Coinbase Staking Order After Three Years first appeared on...
content:
New Jersey’s securities regulator has withdrawn the 2023 cease-and-desist order that barred Coinbase from offering staking to new customers in the state, ending a three-year standoff that cost residents an estimated $15 million in forgone rewards.

The Bureau of Securities notice, dated Oct. 30 and signed by Acting Bureau Chief Keith A. Alt, rescinds the order and the $5 million penalty that came with it. The withdrawal is without prejudice and without a ruling on the merits. 

Coinbase disclosed the development in its third-quarter report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which states that the regulator informed the company of its intent to rescind on Oct. 29.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said New Jersey users would regain access to staking “very soon.” 

As of Monday, the exchange’s eligibility page continued to list New Jersey among the states where customers cannot stake new principal, and no reopening date has been announced.

How the staking case began

The order traces to June 6, 2023, when the New Jersey bureau joined securities regulators in nine other states — Alabama, California, Illinois, Kentucky, Maryland, South Carolina, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin — in a coordinated action against Coinbase’s staking program. 

The states alleged the service amounted to an unregistered securities offering under state law. 

California led the task force; its action covered more than 600,000 accounts. In July 2023, Coinbase agreed with California, New Jersey, South Carolina and Wisconsin to block customers in those states from staking new funds pending final adjudication. Maryland reached a similar agreement in October 2023. 

Customers who had staked before the orders kept earning rewards, but could not add principal or compound the rewards they received.

The state cases ran parallel to the SEC’s June 2023 lawsuit against Coinbase, which named staking among its claims. The SEC dismissed that case in February 2025. Alabama, Kentucky, Illinois, South Carolina and Vermont dismissed, vacated or withdrew their own actions in March and April 2025. New Jersey is the sixth of the original ten states to step back.

What the withdrawal does and does not do

Rescinding the order ends the restriction on new staking in New Jersey. It does not resolve the underlying legal question. The bureau made no finding on whether Coinbase’s staking program is a security, and the “without prejudice” language preserves its ability to file a new action. Coinbase’s own filing calls the state matters “preliminary” and says an adverse resolution “could have a material impact” on the business.

The filing describes a planned rescission rather than a completed one, which explains the gap between Armstrong’s statement and the unchanged eligibility page. The change for New Jersey residents arrives when Coinbase updates its systems, not when the notice was signed.

Coinbase has framed the state restrictions as a competitive disadvantage. In an April 2025 post, the company’s Ryan VanGrack argued the orders singled out one provider while residents could stake through other platforms. Coinbase put forgone rewards across the four restricted states at more than $130 million as of October 2025.

Four states remain. California, Maryland and Wisconsin continue to bar new staking on Coinbase while their cases proceed; Washington permits staking but is pursuing a $4 million fine. Coinbase estimates California residents have missed more than $89 million in rewards since 2023. 

The decision lands as federal policy has shifted but not settled. The SEC has withdrawn from the registration-based cases it brought in 2023, and the CLARITY market structure bill passed the House in 2025 but stalled in the Senate. State securities regulators are not bound by the SEC’s enforcement priorities, which is why the staking cases outlived the federal one by more than a year and a half. 

A future SEC, or a future bureau chief in Trenton, could revisit the question.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $77,500 as Midterm Voting Begins
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $77,500 as Midterm Voting Begins
Bitcoin price trades near $77,500 as midterm voting begins, pressured by a record $6.3 billion Binance hack, ETF outflows, a Fed leaning toward a December hike and oil above $100 on Iran tensions.
This post Bitcoin Price Tr...
content:
Bitcoin price traded near $77,500 on Tuesday morning as polls opened for the U.S. midterm elections, down about .6% on the day and roughly $30,000 below its price one year ago, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. 

The vote decides control of Congress and, with it, the fate of the CLARITY Act, the market structure bill that passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. 

Prediction markets on Kalshi give Democrats a 94% chance of taking the House and 74% for the Senate. A Democratic Senate would likely put Sen. Elizabeth Warren in line to chair the Banking Committee. If Congress does not act before the new session convenes on Jan. 3, the bill dies and must be reintroduced.

Crypto groups spent more than $200 million on the midterms, CNBC reported. Analysts at TD Cowen see a Democratic sweep as the most probable outcome and the least favorable one for the industry; a divided Congress, in their view, leaves room for a narrower deal.

A week of selling

The bitcoin price action into the vote has been one-directional. Bitcoin price opened November near $78,500 and has lost about $2,000 since. October closed down about 7%, the second straight October decline. 

On Oct. 28, after a hawkish Federal Reserve hold and weak earnings from Alphabet and Samsung, the price fell below $80,000 for the first time in weeks, with about $356 million in leveraged positions liquidated.

The larger shock came the next day. On Oct. 29, attackers the FBI attributes to North Korea drained about $6.3 billion from Binance’s hot wallets, the largest crypto theft on record. 

Bitcoin price held strong but fell about 4% on Friday and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $643.3 million that day, their largest single-day outflow since June 25, according to SoSoValue data. Another $399 million left on Monday.

Bitcoin recovered to $78,491 late Sunday before sliding again on Monday and Tuesday. Traders are watching support between $76,264 and $76,476, which lines up with the 200-day exponential moving average. Below that sits the September low of $74,967. 

The 50-day EMA near $80,800 is the first resistance above. 

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 37 on Monday, in “fear” territory. 

Oil, Iran and a Fed that can hike

The macro backdrop offers little support. The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on Oct. 28 by a 10-2 vote, with two officials dissenting in favor of a hike, after raising rates in September for the first time since July 2023. 

Polymarket puts the odds of a December hike near 71%. September PCE inflation ran at 3.6% year over year and third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace.

 The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.36% in early October, its highest since 2002, before easing to about 4.91% on Monday.

Energy sits at the center of the inflation picture. Brent crude fell 7.7% on Monday to $104.66 a barrel after Iran and the U.S. signaled openness to talks, its biggest one-day drop since July, CNBC reported. 

The move reversed in part on Tuesday, with Brent back near $106.60 after reports of a U.S. strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island. Disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has kept crude above $100 and headline inflation elevated, which keeps the Fed on a tightening path.

Equities have added to the pressure. The Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Friday, its worst day since June, after results from Intel and Amazon raised questions about AI capital spending, and lost 5.3% in October. Bitcoin price has moved with technology stocks through the selloff rather than against them.

What comes next for bitcoin price 

The calendar is full. The October jobs report lands Friday, with consensus near 65,000 after September’s 29,000. October CPI follows on Nov. 10 and the Fed’s next decision on Dec. 9. Binance’s next proof-of-reserves snapshot is due Wednesday.

title: Cyprus-Linked 'Crime-as-a-Service' Operation Dismantled in Multi-National Police Raid
summary:
A coordinated international law enforcement operation has dismantled the technical infrastructure of a sweeping investment fraud scheme estimated to have defrauded victims in more than 50 countries of at least €4 million.
The operation targeted a "crime-as-a-service" network. Operating primarily out...
content:
2026-11-03T15:20:42.211+02:00

Tuesday, 03/11/2026 | 13:20 GMT by Adonis Adoni

  • The investment fraud scheme, which operated primarily out of Cyprus and Israel, involved fraudulent trading platforms and the sale of personal data to call center operators.
  • The scheme is believed to have siphoned at least €4 million from targeted victims spanning over 50 countries.

A coordinated international law enforcement operation has dismantled the technical infrastructure of a sweeping investment fraud scheme estimated to have defrauded victims in more than 50 countries of at least €4 million.

The operation targeted a "crime-as-a-service" network. Operating primarily out of Cyprus and Israel, it allegedly provided fraudulent trading platforms, abused affiliated marketing channels to attract victims, and sold their personal data to various call center operators based in Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia.

Led by the Itzehoe Public Prosecutor's Office in Germany, with support from Europol and Eurojust, the action on Tuesday resulted in the arrest of seven suspects and the seizure of more than 100 servers.

Authorities executed search warrants across 17 locations in multiple countries, securing evidence and freezing assets.

The arrested individuals are currently facing extradition to Germany.

The Mechanics of the Fraud

The scheme relied on deceptive affiliate marketing campaigns promising fast, substantial returns on cryptocurrency, foreign exchange and stock investments. These online advertisements were used to harvest personal data from interested individuals, which was then sold to the networks operating the call centers.

According to Europol, scammers would contact potential victims and persuade them to make a small initial investment. To establish credibility, the fraudulent platforms displayed fictitious profits.

Operating under the guise of legitimate brokers, the suspects allegedly used high-pressure sales tactics to convince victims to transfer increasingly larger sums.

When victims eventually attempted to withdraw their funds, the operators deployed delaying tactics before cutting off contact entirely, leaving investors with total losses.

A Four-Year Investigation

Tuesday’s raids mark the culmination of a four-year investigation that began with a single complaint. In 2022, a German couple reported to authorities that they were unable to withdraw funds they had invested through what appeared to be an online trading platform.

That initial report triggered a multi-year probe featuring earlier interventions in 2022 and 2025. Data and evidence recovered during those previous actions allowed authorities to map the network, ultimately identifying the central infrastructure providers and their links to the regional call centers.

This latest operation highlights an escalating trend of European authorities targeting the logistical networks behind investment scams.

In November 2025, authorities dismantled a €700 million scam operation with links to Limassol, while a 2026 Europol-supported raid resulted in the arrest of three suspects in Cyprus over an alleged crypto investment fraud network operating a call-center-style business.

  • Join financial leaders at Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 on Nov 24!

The countdown to Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 continues. On 24 November 2026, the financial services industry will return to Old Billingsgate for the Summit’s 15th edition, bringing together senior decision-makers, industry leaders and professionals for a focused day of networking, knowledge-sharing and business development.

Representatives from Institutional Trading, Technology Providers, Retail Brokers, Fintech and Payments will come together to strengthen professional relationships, explore new opportunities and discuss the developments shaping their industry.

For those looking to expand their networks, reconnect with existing partners and discover new business opportunities, the Summit offers a dedicated environment to make meaningful connections.

Make the Most of Your Experience in London

Meet Your Next Business Partner

The Summit brings together C-level executives, founders, directors and senior professionals from across financial services, creating opportunities to connect face-to-face with the people driving the industry forward.

Whether the goal is to establish new partnerships, explore potential collaborations or strengthen existing business relationships, these conversations can be an important starting point for future opportunities.

Hear What's Shaping the Industry

The financial services landscape continues to evolve, creating new challenges and opportunities for businesses across the sector.

Through industry discussions and expert debates, Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 will provide a platform to explore current developments, exchange perspectives and gain valuable industry intelligence.

Attendees can engage with the topics influencing their markets and take away insights relevant to their business strategies.

Turn Introductions Into Opportunities With Business Connect

Building connections is only the beginning. Business Connect helps attendees make the most of their time at the Summit by facilitating relevant business conversations.

From meeting prospective clients to reconnecting with existing partners, attendees can use Business Connect to identify valuable contacts and arrange conversations aligned with their professional goals.

With the right people in one place, the Summit creates opportunities to turn introductions into meaningful business relationships.

Start Connecting Before the Summit

Networking begins one day before the main event with the Opening Networking Blitz at The Folly on 23 November 2026.

The pre-Summit gathering gives attendees an opportunity to meet fellow professionals, establish initial connections and begin their Summit experience ahead of the main event at Old Billingsgate.

It is an opportunity to start conversations early and make the most of the time spent in London.

One Focused Day. New Connections. New Opportunities.

As Finance Magnates Summit London celebrates its 15th edition, the focus remains on bringing together the people, companies and conversations that matter to the financial services industry.

From face-to-face networking and industry discussions to targeted business meetings, the Summit offers one dedicated day to strengthen relationships, exchange knowledge and explore what comes next.

With 24 November approaching, now is the time to plan your visit and secure your place among the professionals gathering in London.

title: Zlatan and Fury Arrive, XTB’s Sign-Ups Hold Steady
summary:
XTB signed up about 5% more new clients in October's first 27 days than a year earlier, despite running what it calls its biggest advertising campaign. Year-on-year growth had reached 51% in the third quarter.
The company reported more than 100,600 new clients for the period alongside its third-quar...
content:
2026-11-03T14:36:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 03/11/2026 | 12:36 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The broker’s biggest ad campaign began October 1, and new clients rose 5% year on year in the first 27 days.
  • Omar Arnaout said he would not worry, pointing to quieter markets and the tax-account season still ahead.

XTB signed up about 5% more new clients in October's first 27 days than a year earlier, despite running what it calls its biggest advertising campaign. Year-on-year growth had reached 51% in the third quarter.

The company reported more than 100,600 new clients for the period alongside its third-quarter results on Wednesday. In the same 27 days of 2025, it added 95,900, according to its results report from a year ago.

October's intake still runs above XTB's own target. At about 3,700 new clients a day, it compares with a 2026 goal of 250,000 to 290,000 a quarter, or roughly 2,700 to 3,200 a day, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation. For 2025, the goal was 150,000 to 210,000 a quarter.

XTB ended September with 3.14 million clients, 1.57 million of them active, up 70.3% from a year earlier.

London's trading industry is coming home!

October Kept the Third Quarter's Pace

Measured per day, October looks like the summer months, not the start of the year. XTB added 335,704 clients in the third quarter, or about 3,650 a day, after 333,292 in the second.

The first quarter was faster. XTB added about 370,000 clients between January and March, roughly 4,100 a day, and the first half as a whole brought a record 703,333.

That puts October's daily rate 2% above the third quarter's and about 9% below the first quarter's, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

The annual comparison also got harder. In the third quarter of 2025, XTB signed up 221,762 clients, about 2,400 a day, before October last year lifted the rate to roughly 3,550. The 51% growth of the latest quarter was measured against that slower base.

A Campaign After a Marketing Pullback

Omar Arnaout, the chief executive, said at Thursday's results conference that advertising does not always bring more clients straight away. He was answering a question about why sign-ups flattened despite the campaign.

XTB ran almost no outdoor campaigns in the third quarter, apart from one in the United Arab Emirates, and toned down marketing elsewhere, Arnaout said. Sign-ups still stayed close to first-half levels, which he put down to work the company had done earlier.

"I wouldn't worry about that flattening," Arnaout said.

He expects client numbers to rise as markets get busier and as the season approaches for tax-advantaged accounts, such as Poland's IKE retirement accounts. Markets were much quieter in the third quarter than in the first half, he added.

Marketing spending reached PLN 187.3 million (about $47.7 million) in the third quarter, up PLN 45.8 million from a year earlier, though it fell from the second quarter as XTB cut online advertising. Total operating costs rose 23.2% to PLN 397.6 million.

Per new client, that is about PLN 558, down from about PLN 638 a year earlier, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

The October push is larger. The campaign with footballer Zlatan Ibrahimovic and boxer Tyson Fury started on October 1 and runs on four continents, and XTB expects 2026 marketing costs to rise about 50% from last year.

Polish Accounts Had Already Slowed

XTB drew 5.5 million organic visits to its websites from Europe in the third quarter, third among brokers behind OANDA and eToro, FM Intelligence's heat map shows.

At home, the slowdown started earlier in the year. XTB opened 68,300 Polish accounts in January and just over 51,000 in February, according to depository data, before monthly additions fell below 50,000 in April.

It added 48,226 in May, taking its domestic total to 1,087,740 accounts. That is more than double the 560,967 held by second-placed mBank's brokerage arm.

XTB signed up about 5% more new clients in October's first 27 days than a year earlier, despite running what it calls its biggest advertising campaign. Year-on-year growth had reached 51% in the third quarter.

The company reported more than 100,600 new clients for the period alongside its third-quarter results on Wednesday. In the same 27 days of 2025, it added 95,900, according to its results report from a year ago.

October's intake still runs above XTB's own target. At about 3,700 new clients a day, it compares with a 2026 goal of 250,000 to 290,000 a quarter, or roughly 2,700 to 3,200 a day, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation. For 2025, the goal was 150,000 to 210,000 a quarter.

XTB ended September with 3.14 million clients, 1.57 million of them active, up 70.3% from a year earlier.

London's trading industry is coming home!

October Kept the Third Quarter's Pace

Measured per day, October looks like the summer months, not the start of the year. XTB added 335,704 clients in the third quarter, or about 3,650 a day, after 333,292 in the second.

The first quarter was faster. XTB added about 370,000 clients between January and March, roughly 4,100 a day, and the first half as a whole brought a record 703,333.

That puts October's daily rate 2% above the third quarter's and about 9% below the first quarter's, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

The annual comparison also got harder. In the third quarter of 2025, XTB signed up 221,762 clients, about 2,400 a day, before October last year lifted the rate to roughly 3,550. The 51% growth of the latest quarter was measured against that slower base.

A Campaign After a Marketing Pullback

Omar Arnaout, the chief executive, said at Thursday's results conference that advertising does not always bring more clients straight away. He was answering a question about why sign-ups flattened despite the campaign.

XTB ran almost no outdoor campaigns in the third quarter, apart from one in the United Arab Emirates, and toned down marketing elsewhere, Arnaout said. Sign-ups still stayed close to first-half levels, which he put down to work the company had done earlier.

"I wouldn't worry about that flattening," Arnaout said.

He expects client numbers to rise as markets get busier and as the season approaches for tax-advantaged accounts, such as Poland's IKE retirement accounts. Markets were much quieter in the third quarter than in the first half, he added.

Marketing spending reached PLN 187.3 million (about $47.7 million) in the third quarter, up PLN 45.8 million from a year earlier, though it fell from the second quarter as XTB cut online advertising. Total operating costs rose 23.2% to PLN 397.6 million.

Per new client, that is about PLN 558, down from about PLN 638 a year earlier, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

The October push is larger. The campaign with footballer Zlatan Ibrahimovic and boxer Tyson Fury started on October 1 and runs on four continents, and XTB expects 2026 marketing costs to rise about 50% from last year.

Polish Accounts Had Already Slowed

XTB drew 5.5 million organic visits to its websites from Europe in the third quarter, third among brokers behind OANDA and eToro, FM Intelligence's heat map shows.

At home, the slowdown started earlier in the year. XTB opened 68,300 Polish accounts in January and just over 51,000 in February, according to depository data, before monthly additions fell below 50,000 in April.

It added 48,226 in May, taking its domestic total to 1,087,740 accounts. That is more than double the 560,967 held by second-placed mBank's brokerage arm.

title: Anthropic CEO Warns AI Could Wipe Out 50% of White-Collar Jobs Within 5 Years
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says rapid advances in artificial intelligence could disrupt half of entry-level white-collar jobs within one to five years.
content:
Skip to content

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says rapid advances in artificial intelligence could disrupt half of entry-level white-collar jobs within one to five years.

The warning highlights growing concerns about AI-driven automation across finance, consulting, technology, and legal services, where businesses increasingly rely on intelligent systems to handle tasks previously assigned to junior employees.

AI Advancements Put Entry-Level White-Collar Jobs at Risk

Speaking in a Fox News interview published on May 19, 2026, Amodei described how quickly artificial intelligence capabilities have improved, warning that the technology is approaching a level where it can take on more complex professional responsibilities.

“Two years ago, it was at the level of a smart high school student; now it’s probably at the level of a smart college student and reaching beyond that,” he said.

Anthropic’s data indicates that 75% of businesses are already using AI to automate entire workflows rather than simply assisting employees with routine tasks. Source: @Damir_Akaza/X

The Anthropic CEO identified routine knowledge-based activities, including document summaries, brainstorming, and financial report preparation, as tasks where AI systems are becoming increasingly capable. These responsibilities often form the foundation of entry-level positions, particularly in industries that depend heavily on research, analysis, and document processing.

Amodei warned that AI could initially support employees before taking over a larger share of their responsibilities.

“Things like summarizing a document, brainstorming, putting together a financial report, makes me worry a lot that entry-level jobs in areas like finance, consulting, tech, many, many other areas like that, entry-level white-collar work,” he said.

He added that these positions could eventually be replaced by AI systems as their capabilities improve.

The executive also acknowledged uncertainty surrounding the pace of adoption but warned that significant employment changes could emerge relatively quickly.

“I would not be surprised if somewhere between one and five years, we started to see big effects here,” Amodei said.

He described the potential consequences as a “serious employment crisis” if the traditional pipeline into professional careers begins to contract.

AI Automation Is Moving Beyond Basic Workplace Assistance

The concerns extend beyond individual productivity tools. Businesses are increasingly exploring AI agents capable of executing multiple stages of a workflow with limited human intervention.

Anthropic’s September 2025 Economic Index report offers insight into this transition. The company analyzed its first-party application programming interface (API) traffic and found that 77% of business uses involved automation patterns, compared with approximately 50% of interactions on Claude’s consumer platform.

Amodei says AI is advancing toward graduate-level capabilities, accelerating the shift from employee assistance to routine task replacement. Source: Damir Akaza via X

The distinction is important because API-based business applications allow organizations to integrate AI capabilities directly into their existing software and operational systems. Instead of simply asking a chatbot to summarize information, companies can use these integrations to delegate complete tasks.

Anthropic’s findings suggest that businesses are increasingly treating AI as an operational tool rather than relying exclusively on human-AI collaboration.

Its 2026 State of AI Agents report provides further evidence of this shift. A survey of more than 500 technical leaders found that 57% of participating organizations already deployed AI agents for multistage workflows. Meanwhile, 81% planned to pursue more complex AI applications during 2026.

These applications include research, data analysis, report generation, and internal process automation.

Such developments could change how organizations structure their departments. Tasks previously divided among several junior employees may increasingly be handled by automated systems, leaving smaller teams responsible for reviewing results, managing operations and making decisions.

However, automation adoption does not automatically translate into an equivalent number of job cuts. Companies must also account for implementation costs, accuracy, regulatory requirements, and the need for human oversight.

Anthropic’s Own Hiring Patterns Reveal an Early Shift

Anthropic’s internal employment data provides another perspective on how AI adoption could reshape corporate hiring.

In an October 16, 2026 research report titled How Employment Is Changing at Anthropic, the company examined its hiring patterns, workforce composition, productivity, and internal use of AI agents.

Anthropic’s observed-exposure metric compares AI’s theoretical job-task capabilities with actual usage, showing Claude handles 33% of computer and math tasks despite a potential 94% coverage. Source: @thesupermannx via X

The research found that junior-level employees accounted for 14% of Anthropic’s technical workforce, down from 21% in early 2025. The share of junior employees among new technical hires declined even further, falling from 27% to 9%.

Anthropic attributed part of the change to improved AI capabilities, particularly in software development, where employees increasingly delegate coding and debugging tasks to AI agents.

The research also found that around one-third of machine-learning managers and one-fifth of software-engineering managers reported hiring fewer employees because of AI in an April 2026 survey.

However, the findings do not indicate that Anthropic has stopped expanding its technical workforce. The company’s absolute technical headcount continued growing, while hiring in sales, finance, and recruiting increased at a faster pace.

The report also described changes in the responsibilities of existing employees. Workers increasingly spend time directing AI agents, checking their output, and building tools that help coordinate automated processes.

This development suggests that AI adoption could reshape job requirements even when positions remain available. Employees may increasingly need skills in critical thinking, decision-making, and managing automated systems rather than focusing exclusively on routine technical execution.

AI Job Displacement Remains an Uncertain Outlook

Despite growing automation capabilities, evidence of widespread AI-driven unemployment remains limited.

Anthropic’s March 2026 labor market study introduced an occupational exposure measure combining theoretical AI capabilities with actual usage patterns. It found that computer and mathematical occupations had the potential for AI to accelerate 94% of their tasks, yet observed AI coverage accounted for approximately 33%.

This gap indicates that technical capability does not automatically translate into widespread workplace replacement. Legal requirements, software integration, organizational processes, and human verification can all slow adoption.

Independent research has identified potential pressure on younger workers entering highly exposed occupations.

A Stanford Digital Economy Lab study, revised in August 2026, analyzed payroll information covering millions of US workers through June. It found that employment among workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed occupations was 19% below the level it would have reached if it had followed employment trends among less-exposed peers.

The researchers found that reduced hiring, rather than increased employee separations, accounted for much of the difference. However, they cautioned that the findings represent early indicators rather than definitive evidence that AI caused the employment gap. The study also found no evidence of widespread economy-wide job displacement.

Similarly, the Yale Budget Lab’s October 14, 2026 labor market update found no clear evidence of large-scale employment disruption associated with AI in its analysis of September employment data.

These findings suggest that the immediate challenge may be a slowdown in recruitment opportunities for younger workers rather than mass layoffs across the entire white-collar workforce.

Preparing for an AI-Driven Labor Market

Amodei believes businesses, workers, and governments must begin addressing the employment risks associated with increasingly capable AI systems.

During the Fox News interview, he argued that stopping technological development would be difficult because of international competition, particularly between the United States and China. Instead, he emphasized the importance of preparing workers and measuring the economic consequences of AI adoption.

He also suggested that governments may eventually need to consider policies that help distribute the economic benefits of AI more broadly, including the possibility of taxing AI companies.

For employees, the transition could require adapting to a workplace where AI handles a growing share of routine digital responsibilities. Familiarity with prompting alone may not be enough as businesses adopt autonomous agents capable of performing interconnected tasks.

Understanding how to integrate AI into professional workflows, evaluate its output, and oversee automated processes could become increasingly important across several industries.

Nevertheless, the long-term consequences will depend on how quickly companies deploy these systems, how much human supervision remains necessary, and whether new employment opportunities emerge alongside automation.

Amodei’s warning places the future of entry-level white-collar employment at the center of the AI debate. Whether his projection materializes remains uncertain, but the changing hiring patterns and growing adoption of AI agents indicate that businesses are already reconsidering how professional work gets done.

title: Provably Fair: The Crypto Gaming Platforms Showcasing the Industry’s Latest Innovation
summary:
When it comes to transparency, crypto gaming platforms are placing one aspect at the heart of their efforts: provably fair technology. There was once a time when platforms would tell
The post Provably Fair: The Crypto Gaming Platforms Showcasing the Industry’s Latest Innovation appeared first on Cry...
content:
When it comes to transparency, crypto gaming platforms are placing one aspect at the heart of their efforts: provably fair technology. There was once a time when platforms would tell players to trust that every result is random. Now, with these systems, there’s a way for them to verify outcomes independently. By applying this technology to their original games, it combines familiar gaming formats with a more transparent approach to game results.

The following crypto platforms are leading the way in showcasing the industry’s latest innovation.

  • Duel
  • Thrill
  • Winna
  • Yeet

Duel

At the forefront of this movement is Duel. Play Duel’s provably fair online games, and you’ll see it is possible to verify the outcomes of its games. That means you can see everything was generated fairly and not simply accept the platform’s word. Before a round, Duel generates a server seed. This is joined by a player-provided client seed and nonce, which increases with each round. It also publishes a SHA-256 hash of the server seed before play, creating a commitment that can be checked later.

After the game, Duel reveals the unhashed server seed. You can compare it with the original hash and verify that the combined seeds and nonce produce the recorded result. This hands you a practical way to check the outcome generation process, with a built-in verifier making the process more accessible. The system applies to each of the 12 “Duel Originals”. Those games also stand out for their 100% RTP, which removes the platform’s mathematical advantage. A one-of-a-kind aspect you won’t find elsewhere, it shows Duel goes to the next level for fair gameplay.

Thrill

Thrill also applies provably fair mechanics to its own in-house games. From Dice to Crash, these titles stick with clear outcomes and straightforward rules. That makes them a natural fit for systems that allow players to check how results are generated. Provably fair technology, naturally, adds a verification layer to the gaming experience. Then with Thrill’s XP progression system and weekly races, there are other reasons for players to return.

Winna

Provably fair is also part of the original games found at Winna. From revealing tiles in Mines to watching a ball bounce through Plinko’s pegs, these in-house titles keep it simple with a decision- or chance-based outcome. The value of provably fair technology here is that players have a way to check results on their own. Like Duel, Winna combines these games with a wider crypto gaming platform and sports-related features for multiple interactive options.

Yeet

Combining sports-related features and crypto gaming with its own originals, Yeet includes in-house creations like Dice and Plinko. As these simple formats place the outcome at the center of the experience, transparency is a key aspect. With its provably fair technology implementation, players gain a method for checking game results. Its originals provide an alternative to its wider selection of third-party titles, while the sports-related section expands the platform beyond its original games.

Provably fair technology gives players a way to verify game outcomes. However, it’s important to highlight that it doesn’t guarantee winning. Even if you check ten wins or ten losses in a row, it plays no part in the next result.

title: What to Do If Your Crypto Card Is Lost, Stolen, or Hacked
summary:
You reach for your wallet and the card is gone. Or worse, your phone buzzes with a payment you did not make. With a normal bank card, you would call
The post What to Do If Your Crypto Card Is Lost, Stolen, or Hacked appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
You reach for your wallet and the card is gone. Or worse, your phone buzzes with a payment you did not make. With a normal bank card, you would call the bank and move on. With a crypto card, the stakes can feel higher, because crypto payments are hard or impossible to reverse.

The good news is that most crypto card problems are fixable if you act quickly and in the right order. The key is understanding what was actually exposed, because a lost card and a hacked wallet are very different problems. Here is exactly what to do in each case.

  • First, Figure Out What Is Actually at Risk
  • If Your Card Is Lost or Stolen
  • If Someone Is Using Your Card Online
  • If Your Account or Wallet Is Hacked
  • Beware of Recovery Scams
  • How to Prevent It Happening Again
  • Frequently Asked Questions

First, Figure Out What Is Actually at Risk

Before you panic, separate the card from the crypto behind it.

SituationWhat is exposedUrgency
Physical card lostThe card number and limitsHigh, but contained
Card details stolen onlineCard paymentsHigh, but contained
App or account login compromisedYour card balance and settingsVery high
Wallet seed phrase exposedEvery coin in that walletCritical

A lost plastic card is usually the least dangerous of these. Someone holding it can try to make card payments, but they cannot empty your wallet with it. A leaked seed phrase is the opposite. Whoever has it controls your funds, and no card freeze will stop them.

If Your Card Is Lost or Stolen

Speed matters most in the first few minutes.

  1. Freeze the card in the app. Nearly every crypto card app has an instant freeze toggle. Use it before anything else, since you can unfreeze it if the card turns up.
  2. Check recent transactions. Look for anything you did not make, and screenshot it.
  3. Contact support. Report the card lost or stolen through the app or the issuer’s official support channel, never a number from a search ad.
  4. Order a replacement. A new card comes with a new number, and the old one is cancelled.
  5. Use the virtual card meanwhile. Many providers issue a virtual card you can add to Apple Pay or Google Pay right away.

Cards that spend directly from your own wallet carry an extra advantage here. With a self-custody Crypto Debit Card, your coins stay in the wallet you control rather than in a separate card account, so a lost card does not hand anyone your funds. Freezing the card cuts off spending, and the crypto never moved. 

If Someone Is Using Your Card Online

Unauthorized charges mean your card details have leaked, often through a breached shop, a phishing page, or malware.

    • Freeze the card and request a new number
    • Report each unauthorized payment to the issuer and ask about dispute options
  • Change the password on your card app and turn on two-factor authentication
  • Scan your devices for malware, and remove browser extensions you do not recognize

Card-network payments sometimes have dispute processes, but support varies widely between crypto card providers. Report quickly, because most dispute windows are short.

If Your Account or Wallet Is Hacked

This is the serious scenario, and it needs a different response.

If your card app login was compromised, change the password immediately, revoke all active sessions, and reset two-factor authentication from a device you trust. Then contact support to lock the account while you investigate.

If your wallet seed phrase or private key was exposed, act as if the wallet is already lost. Create a brand-new wallet with a new seed phrase on a clean device, and move any remaining funds into it right away. Then reconnect your card to the new wallet. Do not try to “secure” the old wallet. Once a seed phrase leaks, that wallet can never be trusted again.

Beware of Recovery Scams

Right after a theft is when the second scam usually arrives. People who post about lost crypto online are quickly targeted by “recovery experts” promising to trace and return stolen funds for an upfront fee. They cannot. The FTC’s guide on what to know about cryptocurrency and scams notes that crypto payments typically cannot be reversed, and that anyone guaranteeing to recover your money is a red flag.

Report real theft to your card provider, the police, and the FTC or your country’s equivalent. Never pay someone who contacts you offering to get your crypto back.

How to Prevent It Happening Again

A few habits make a big difference:

  • Turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, not SMS
  • Never store your seed phrase in photos, notes apps, or cloud storage
  • Set spending limits and transaction alerts in your card app
  • Use the virtual card for online shopping and keep the physical card for in-person payments
  • Keep most of your crypto in a separate wallet from your spending balance

If you are still deciding which card to use, it helps to start by comparing the top crypto cards on security features as well as fees and rewards. Instant freeze controls, real-time alerts, and self-custody spending are worth as much as a higher cashback rate on the day something goes wrong.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can someone steal my crypto with just my card?

Usually not. A physical card or its number can be used for card payments within its limits, but it does not give access to your wallet. Your seed phrase and app login are the real keys to your funds.

Can I get my money back after an unauthorized crypto card payment?

Sometimes. Card-network payments may be eligible for a dispute, depending on your provider’s policy. Report the charge immediately, since dispute windows are often short.

Should I freeze or cancel my card?

Freeze it first. Freezing is instant and reversible if the card turns up. Cancel and replace it once you confirm it is truly lost or that the details were stolen, and update any subscriptions linked to the old number.

Is it safe to use a recovery service for stolen crypto?

No. Services that promise to recover stolen crypto for an upfront fee are almost always scams. Report the theft to your provider and the authorities instead.

title: Nvidia, Nike Join 50 Companies Blocking OKX–ICE Stock Token Push
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Nvidia, Nike Join 50 Companies Blocking OKX–ICE Stock Token Push
Fifty companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft and JPMorgan, have blocked OKX and ICE from tokenizing their shares under the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption.
This post Nvidia, Nike Join 50 Companies Blocking OKX–ICE Stoc...
content:
Fifty public companies have now objected to having their shares tokenized on OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), as the venue’s first 30-day notice window closes Tuesday.

The venue’s Oct. 30 notice added 12 objectors, including Nvidia, Costco, Nike, Micron and Reddit. They join Microsoft, Alphabet, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Walmart, Broadcom, Verizon and Intel, among others. Of the 62 companies OKXICE initially proposed to tokenize, 43, or about 69%, have objected, according to a CoinDesk tally.

The list has grown fast: nine objectors on Oct. 15, 16 on Oct. 19, 38 on Oct. 28 and 50 two days later.

How the opt-out works

The objections stem from the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued Sept. 17, which lets tokenized securities venues (TSVs) trade blockchain versions of U.S. stocks through automated market makers without registering as exchanges. When an unaffiliated third party tokenizes a company’s stock, the venue must notify the issuer, which then has 30 days to object in writing. Silence counts as consent, and the order offers no way to object after the window closes.

OKXICE plans 24/7 trading of tokens backed one-for-one by shares, paired against stablecoins such as USDC in permissioned pools on OKX’s X Layer blockchain.

The objecting companies have not given reasons. JPMorgan said it remains encouraged by tokenization but wants to be thoughtful about how its shares are represented and traded. “Given how easy the opt-out is, the list of objectors is likely to keep growing,” Olivia Vande Woude, head of tokenization at Ava Labs, said.

Nasdaq’s role

The fight has also taken on a competitive edge. An executive at a Nasdaq-listed company told Crypto in America that a Nasdaq representative urged the company to object and offered a call to explain why. Nasdaq declined to comment on the claim but reiterated that TSVs are not the best path to tokenization.

Nasdaq argues that venues outside the National Market System could fragment liquidity and lack real-time best-price display and consolidated-tape reporting. It is building its own issuer-centric Nasdaq Equity Token with Kraken, targeted for the second quarter of 2027.

A full-page Wall Street Journal ad urging CEOs to opt out, headlined “YOUR STOCK. THEIR TOKENS. YOUR PROBLEM.,” linked to Nasdaq’s FAQ via QR code. Conservative-leaning nonprofit Common Sense Leadership Fund paid for it. Nasdaq said it had no connection to the ad and never funded the group.

OKXICE co-chair and former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo has called the objections a “natural response.” 

“We are at the very beginning of the rollout of fundamentally different market structure,” he said last week.

For context, a tokenized stock is a blockchain token backed one-for-one by a real share, which a third party holds. OKXICE lets it trade around the clock against stablecoins like USDC. Under the SEC’s Innovation Exemption, the venue can list these tokens without the issuing company’s consent, unless the company objects within 30 days.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Pghinvestment and the Retail Investors the Market Was Not Built For
summary: The retail investor arriving today looks very little like the one most trading platforms were originally designed around. They are younger, far more likely to be based outside the traditional financial centres, and in a great many cases they came to markets through digital assets, not through a brok...
content:
Skip to content

The retail investor arriving today looks very little like the one most trading platforms were originally designed around. They are younger, far more likely to be based outside the traditional financial centres, and in a great many cases they came to markets through digital assets, not through a broker or an adviser. What they frequently do not arrive with is formal financial education.

That is not a criticism of them. It is a description of a market that opened up faster than the teaching around it did, and it leaves platforms holding a question they did not previously have to answer: what do you owe someone who is capable, motivated and underprepared all at once.

Most of the industry has answered that question with content. Webinars, glossaries, a learning tab nobody opens twice.

The more telling answer is structural. It shows up in how an account behaves, not in what the marketing says about education.

What the participation data actually shows

The World Economic Forum, in its Global Retail Investor Outlook, describes a new wave of participants drawn from groups the industry historically underserved, including younger investors and people in emerging markets, and names limited financial education and the complexity of evolving technology among the obstacles they meet. The audience is widening in exactly the places where support has always been thinnest.

The World Federation of Exchanges reaches a complementary conclusion from the market side. Reviewing retail trading across its member exchanges, it finds that retail participation improves liquidity and the depth of the order book, while stating directly that it may increase volatility and must be complemented with strong investor protection policies. More participation is only a good outcome when something is built to carry it.

Learning without paying for the lesson

This is where Pghinvestment has made a choice that reads as a product decision but functions as an educational one. Its practice environment runs on the conditions a funded account actually sees, so the pricing and execution a client meets while testing are the ones waiting for them afterwards.

That distinction matters more than it sounds. A rehearsal that flatters the trader is not neutral. It is misleading, because it produces a confidence the market never agreed to.

Experts at Pghinvestment treat that fidelity as the whole point of the feature, not a technical detail buried inside it, which is why the practice environment sits alongside the live Pghinvestment platform rather than behind a beginner label.

The Pghinvestment entry point works in the same direction. An account can be opened without committing an amount a client would genuinely miss, which turns the first months into something a person can afford to be bad at. That is a more realistic model of how trading is actually learned than any curriculum.

Participation before mastery

There is a second route through the preparedness gap, and it is the one Pghinvestment leans on hardest: it does not insist on mastery as the price of entry.

Its managed structures let someone take part while they are still learning, instead of making them wait until they are not. PAMM and MAM arrangements place capital alongside a more experienced trader while the owner keeps sight of what is happening to it, and Copy Trading mirrors selected positions as they occur.

Used well, the Pghinvestment managed structures amount to a form of apprenticeship. A client watching decisions get made on their own balance, in markets they are still reading, learns something a tutorial cannot teach. The framing from Pghinvestment is consistent with that: these structures are presented as a route into participation while understanding builds, not as a reason to stop building it.

One environment, widening scope

There is a quieter benefit in the breadth of the Pghinvestment account range. Currencies, equities, metals, indices, commodities and digital assets sit behind one login, which means a client broadening their exposure is not also learning an unfamiliar system at the same moment they are learning an unfamiliar market.

The thing that changes is the instrument, not the interface. For someone who arrived through digital assets and is now looking at metals or indices for the first time, removing that second layer of unfamiliarity is worth more than it appears on a feature comparison.

Funding runs through card, bank transfer or digital currency, with nothing added by Pghinvestment to make a deposit. Withdrawal thresholds are set low, which keeps the arrangement workable for clients operating at modest size while they find their footing.

Where this leaves the industry

Instrument counts will keep getting longer across the industry, and they will keep mattering less than how a platform behaves in a client’s first six months. The firms that come out of this period with retained clients will be the ones that planned for people learning the job while doing it. Judged on how Pghinvestment has assembled its practice conditions, its managed routes in and its entry pricing, that looks like the assumption it started from.

title: Crypto Fear Index Drops to 30 After Binance Hack as Ethereum ETFs See $1B in Outflows
summary: The Crypto Fear and Greed Index has slipped into fear territory as Binance responds to a $6.3 billion security breach and US spot Ethereum ETFs record heavy October redemptions.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

The Crypto Fear and Greed Index has slipped into fear territory as Binance responds to a $6.3 billion security breach and US spot Ethereum ETFs record heavy October redemptions.

The developments highlight growing caution across cryptocurrency markets, although available data do not establish that the Binance attack directly triggered the Ethereum ETF withdrawals.

Market participants are now monitoring exchange fund flows, institutional investment activity, and cryptocurrency prices for signs of further weakness. The latest Bitcoin (BTC) market data and Ethereum (ETH) price data offer additional context as investors assess the market’s response to the latest developments.

Crypto Fear and Greed Index Falls to 30 After Binance Hack

According to CryptoQuant, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to 30 on October 30, placing market sentiment in the fear zone for the first time since mid-August. The decline followed Binance’s October 29 security breach, which resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion in unauthorized cryptocurrency withdrawals.

Bitcoin’s Fear and Greed Index fell to 30, signaling fear among investors following Binance’s record $6.3 billion hack. Source: @cryptoquant_com via X

Market sentiment had already weakened before the incident. The index fell from 68 on October 22 to 51 by October 29, indicating that investors were becoming increasingly cautious ahead of the exchange’s announcement. Its latest reading of 30 is also 26 points below the 30-day average of 56. CryptoQuant’s historical comparison places the reading below the median of 44, although it remains above the lower quartile of 26.

The FBI attributed the Binance attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group. The exchange’s preliminary investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allegedly provided attackers with access to internal systems used to authorize withdrawals. Binance said it had found no evidence that wallet private keys were exposed.

The scale of the incident triggered an industry-wide recovery effort involving blockchain intelligence firms, law enforcement agencies, and cryptocurrency issuers. Approximately $3 billion in affected assets had been located or frozen through cooperation with industry partners. Binance also said it had covered approximately $6 billion of the estimated losses through its corporate treasury, insurance resources, and Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).

The incident has also raised questions about the security of centralized cryptocurrency exchanges and their internal withdrawal systems. Brave New Coin previously examined the breach, its recovery efforts, and the exchange’s compensation commitment in its report, Binance Confirms $6.3B Security Breach, Freezes $3B in Assets and Pledges Full Compensation.

Ethereum ETFs Record More Than $1 Billion in October Outflows

Institutional investment activity has also weakened, with US spot Ethereum ETFs experiencing substantial net redemptions during October. A report citing Glassnode data identified 23 consecutive trading days of net outflows through October 30, marking the longest reported outflow streak since the funds launched in July 2024.

US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded 23 consecutive days of net outflows through late October 2026, marking their longest withdrawal streak since launching in July 2024. Source: Glassnode via X

The withdrawals extended a period of weaker demand following substantial ETF buying in August and September. October’s net outflows exceeded $1 billion, reversing the previous month’s $832.43 million in net inflows reported by SoSoValue. The pressure remained visible toward the end of the month, when US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded approximately $155.7 million in net outflows on October 30, according to Farside Investors’ daily figures.

Farside-based calculations put the full October net outflow at approximately $1.61 billion. This highlights the scale of the monthly reversal, even as some funds attracted smaller inflows during individual trading sessions.

There is, however, a difference between the reported 23-day Glassnode streak and Farside’s publicly available daily figures. Farside recorded positive aggregate inflows on October 13, October 21, and October 23, with 19 net outflow sessions among October’s 22 trading days. The 23-day figure should therefore be attributed specifically to the Glassnode-tracked series rather than treated as a universally confirmed result across all ETF flow trackers.

The figures nevertheless point to a clear deterioration in monthly demand for US spot Ethereum investment products. ETF net outflows measure the difference between money entering and leaving the funds, rather than the total amount of Ethereum traded in the broader market. They also do not identify individual investors or establish why holders are redeeming their shares.

The reversal is particularly notable because September’s positive flows followed heavy institutional accumulation during the summer. October’s redemptions indicate that demand through traditional investment products has weakened, placing additional pressure on Ethereum’s institutional investment outlook.

Binance Withdrawals Reach $4.72 Billion as Exchange Confidence Faces Pressure

The Binance incident has created another source of concern for cryptocurrency investors, with customers moving substantial amounts of capital away from the exchange after withdrawal services resumed.

According to Reuters, Binance customers withdrew a net $4.72 billion after the exchange reopened withdrawals on November 1. The outflow represented approximately 2.8% of the platform’s assets, while Binance reported that $2.7 billion had also flowed back into the exchange. The latest figure exceeds earlier estimates of approximately $3.6 billion as withdrawals continued to be processed.

Binance restored withdrawals in phases starting at 06:00 UTC on November 1, 2026, processing $4.649B outflows across 15 networks/assets by 15:30 UTC. Source: Binance via X

Binance said withdrawal activity had declined following an initial spike and was stabilizing. The exchange has also maintained that customers will not bear the financial losses associated with the security breach.

The response from market observers has been more measured than the initial withdrawal figures might suggest. Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, told Reuters that the incident had not yet caused widespread panic among customers.

“It has not yet triggered widespread panic or a massive, concentrated withdrawal,” Sun said.

Nevertheless, the incident could influence how institutional investors, market makers, and other financial participants assess cryptocurrency exchange exposure. Security concerns are particularly relevant for organizations responsible for holding customer assets or providing liquidity across multiple trading platforms.

The wider market response has also reflected this caution. Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $643 million in net outflows on October 30, while more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to reporting cited by Reuters. These developments indicate that selling pressure extended beyond Ethereum investment products and the Binance platform.

Ethereum Staking Reaches Record High Despite ETF Redemptions

Despite weaker institutional demand through spot ETFs, Ethereum’s on-chain staking activity has continued to expand. According to Bitwise’s third-quarter staking report, approximately 43.8 million ETH was locked in staking by the end of September, representing around 35.9% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply.

Ethereum staking reached a record 43.8 million ETH in Q3 2026, representing 35.9% of the total supply, according to Bitwise. Source: @BSCNews via X

Net staking inflows reached approximately 1.99 million ETH during the third quarter. This marked the sixth consecutive quarter in which more ETH entered staking than left the network. The increase also established a new record for the amount of Ethereum committed to securing the blockchain.

However, staking growth has not come without changes to investor returns. Bitwise reported that Ethereum’s annualized gross staking yield declined to 2.63% in the third quarter from 2.81% in the previous quarter. The lower yield reflects rewards being distributed across a larger pool of staked ETH.

Ethereum’s price has also remained above $2,200 despite the ETF withdrawals and broader market uncertainty. Historical market data show that ETH traded near $2,245 on October 30 before recovering toward $2,285 by November 2.

The contrasting trends suggest that different groups of Ethereum investors are responding to market conditions in different ways. Investors using exchange-traded products have reduced their exposure, while the amount of ETH committed to network staking has continued to increase.

However, rising staking activity does not establish that existing Ethereum holders are directly absorbing the coins associated with ETF redemptions. ETF flow figures and staking deposits measure separate activities, and the available data do not identify whether the same investors are participating in both.

For the broader cryptocurrency market, the next developments in exchange security, ETF demand, and Ethereum staking will remain important indicators of investor positioning. A sustained recovery in ETF inflows and the Fear and Greed Index could indicate improving confidence, while continued withdrawals would point to persistent caution across traditional crypto investment channels.
