title: Ethereum (ETH) Price Prediction: Whale Longs Surge as $2,200 Demand Zone Puts $3,000 Back in Focus
summary: Ethereum (ETH) price prediction remains at a critical juncture as whale longs surge, ETF outflows persist, and bulls defend the $2,200 demand zone for a potential recovery toward $3,000.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

Ethereum (ETH) price prediction remains at a critical juncture as whale longs surge, ETF outflows persist, and bulls defend the $2,200 demand zone for a potential recovery toward $3,000.

Ethereum is attempting to stabilize after another difficult stretch, with price returning to an area that has repeatedly played an important role in previous market cycles. The broader picture is beginning to split between price weakness and improving fundamentals. According to Brave New Coin, ETH price is trading around $2,291.31, up 1.08% over the past 24 hours.

Ethereum Returns to a Demand Zone Near $2,200

Ethereum is back inside one of the more important areas on its weekly chart. Blockto’s analysis places ETH inside a broad demand zone around $2,100-$2,400, an area that has acted as support during several previous market swings.

ETH price is now trading near $2,290 after testing the lower half of that zone. If buyers continue to defend the area, the first recovery would bring $2,600-$2,700 back into focus, followed by the broader $3,000-$3,200 region where Ethereum previously faced heavier resistance.

The downside scenario becomes more relevant if ETH starts losing the demand zone altogether. In that case, the weekly chart leaves room for a deeper move toward roughly $1,500-$1,600 before another major support area comes into play.

Further out, the chart continues to show the $4,100-$4,700 region as the major higher-timeframe resistance. Ethereum would need to rebuild through several levels before that zone becomes relevant again, but holding the current demand area would be the first step toward restoring that larger structure.

Source: Blockto via X

Whale Longs Build While ETF Pressure Remains High

Ethereum’s positioning data is starting to show a clear split between large traders and institutional fund flows. Merlin The Trader highlights a roughly 368% increase in whale long exposure, with whales now carrying around 3.6 times more long positions than they did in August.

Ethereum whale longs have surged 368% since August, signaling growing bullish positioning. Source: Merlin The Trader via X

That buildup suggests larger market participants are using the recent weakness to increase bullish exposure. Ethereum price is still trading close to its support region, so the increase in whale longs becomes more meaningful if price begins to stabilize and recover from current levels.

Ethereum spot ETFs recorded $155.7 million in outflows on October 30, led by BlackRock’s ETHA. Source: DustyBC via X

The ETF side remains less supportive. U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded approximately $155.7 million in net outflows on October 30, with BlackRock’s ETHA accounting for roughly $76.6 million of that total. Continued withdrawals show that institutional demand through ETF products has not yet matched the bullish positioning seen elsewhere in the market.

Ethereum Staking Adds Support to the Bullish Supply

The split between stronger whale positioning and weaker ETF flows is not the only development shaping Ethereum’s outlook. On the supply side, staking activity has continued to rise, with Cointelegraph reporting that more ETH moved into staking during October than in any previous month. Total staked ETH now stands near 44.2 million.

That trend matters because it reduces the amount of ETH that remains immediately available in the market at the same time whales are increasing long exposure. Even with ETF outflows still acting as a drag, a larger share of supply being locked away can help tighten the market if demand starts to recover.

The combination does not remove the need for price confirmation, but it strengthens the backdrop around the current support zone. If ETF pressure begins to ease while whale longs remain elevated, record staking activity could become another factor supporting a stronger recovery.

Ethereum staking climbed to roughly 44.2 million ETH. Source: Cointelegraph via X.

Ethereum Price Pattern Targeting $3,000

The improving fundamentals around Ethereum are beginning to show up on the chart as well. With whale longs rising and more ETH moving into staking, Max Crypto highlights a potential inverse head-and-shoulders pattern developing near the same demand region ETH price is currently trying to defend.

The right shoulder is still forming, which keeps the pattern unconfirmed for now. A recovery through the neckline around the mid-$2,500s would be the more important development, as that would show buyers are finally turning the recent accumulation and tighter supply conditions into actual price strength.

If that breakout develops, $3,000 becomes the next major level in the recovery path. Until then, the structure remains a developing reversal setup, with the recent lows needing to hold for the bullish pattern to stay intact.

Ethereum is forming a potential inverse head-and-shoulders, with a neckline breakout pointing towards $3,000. Source: Max Crypto via X.

ETH Price Technical Analysis

Ethereum is trying to recover after spending most of October under pressure. The one-month chart shows ETH falling from above $2,650 toward the $2,200 area before buyers finally produced a stronger reaction, with price now back near $2,287.

The latest rebound has improved the very short-term picture, but Ethereum price is still trading below several areas lost during the decline. The first challenge sits around $2,300-$2,350, while a stronger recovery would need to push back through roughly $2,400 before the October downtrend begins to look materially different.

Ethereum price is trading at around $2,287, up 0.92% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

The reaction around the recent low is encouraging, particularly after the increase in trading activity that accompanied the selloff. If ETH price continues building above $2,200 rather than immediately giving back the rebound, the current move could develop into a broader recovery attempt.

Final Thoughts: What’s Next in Q4 2026?

Ethereum enters the remaining part of Q4 with price still recovering from a difficult October, but the setup underneath the market has become more interesting. Whale longs are building, staking continues to remove ETH from the liquid supply, and the chart is beginning to show early reversal possibilities around a historically important demand region. ETF outflows remain the main piece still working against that improvement.

For the broader Ethereum Price Prediction, Q4 becomes more constructive if ETH price can turn the current rebound into acceptance above $2,300-$2,400 and eventually work back toward the mid-$2,000s. That would keep $3,000 relevant later in the quarter, while another loss of the $2,200 region would suggest Ethereum still has more work to do before a durable recovery develops.

title: Silver Price Forecast After the October Fed Decision as December Rate Risks Grow
summary: Prices for silver dipped below $50 per ounce on October 31, continuing a steep decline through the month.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAG

Prices for silver dipped below $50 per ounce on October 31, continuing a steep decline through the month.

Spot silver was $49.1465 and had dropped 5.79% on the day, according to Investing.com. Over the week, the metal depreciated by 8.89%, while it fell by 18.70% from the beginning of October.

The selling came after the Federal Reserve on Oct. 28 raised interest rates in its policy meeting and reignited inflation fears. With the prospect of silver’s recovery being determined by the interplay between monetary policy, political uncertainty and industrial demand before December, investors are now considering all three factors.

October Fed Decision Leaves December Rate Risks Unresolved

On October 28, the Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate policy unchanged at 3.75%–4.00%. The vote was 10-2 to decide, with two policymakers deciding to raise a quarter point. The Fed pointed to “resilient economic activity,” solid productivity and “elevated inflation.

Federal Reserve publishes statement of the FOMC meeting

The ruling did not put an end to hopes for additional narrowing. If inflation continues and economic growth remains robust, then rates may remain high and offer a higher opportunity cost of having no income generated from silver. Rising borrowing costs can also strain industrial demand by reducing economic activity.

The next meeting of the FOMC is December 8-9. Investors will be watching the inflation reading, employment data and the outlook of the policymakers for clues as to the next move. A rate rise would likely put pressure on silver, whereas a rate hold will help its recovery if inflation also slows.

Technical Indicators Show Deepening Selling Pressure

Silver has fallen from just above $53 to around $49.15 on the chart that was provided by Investing.com. The metal dabbled around the $48.90 mark before settling again at the end of the session. During the previous month, it lost 18.70%, and during the past six months, it lost 33.40%.

The silver price was $49.135 on TradingView on October 31, falling 5.81%. The price is trading below its 20-day moving averages, $59.736 and $62.578, respectively. Both were trending down, and that was a continuation of the bearish trend. Source: TradingView

RSI dropped to 23.70, which was below its signal average of 34.34. Readings below 30 typically represent oversold conditions. But oversold readings are not always accompanied by an immediate turnaround, especially during prolonged periods of selling.

The next downside reference is the $48.86 intraday low. Silver may be further trying to break below the level, suggesting a continued decline in the price of the precious metal. A recovery above $50 would signal initial stabilisation, and a recovery of $59.74 would show more that things are going well.

Midterm Elections Add Uncertainty to December’s Silver Outlook

Another market catalyst is coming up on Tuesday, November 3, with the US midterm elections. Congressional changes may impact fiscal talks and trade negotiations as well as investor expectations. But election results are not the sole factor affecting silver prices; their impact is tied to how they affect the dollar, Treasury yields and economic expectations.

Silver has upside potential in November as markets should price in further monetary policy tightening and inflation may hold. Silver is used in the manufacturing sector, so if consumers don’t have the money to invest, continued weakness in industrial demand could pressure prices.

There are two general cases for December.

Should inflation slow and the Fed hint at an end to the rate-hike cycle, silver may find support around the $55 level and continue to rally to the $60 level. If expectations of rates increase and inflation continues to persist, prices may reach the low end of the $48 range or drop further.

These levels are not guaranteed, but depend on the scenarios. Before identifying a rebound, investors need to watch the dollar, real yields, industrial demand and the December Fed decision.

title: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance was able to resume withdrawals for 15 blockchain networks. More than $5.8 billion in net withdrawals were seen over the 24 hours, as tracked by DefiLlama. The
The post Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance was able to resume withdrawals for 15 blockchain networks.
  • More than $5.8 billion in net withdrawals were seen over the 24 hours, as tracked by DefiLlama.
  • The exchange is recovering from the record $6.3 billion crypto theft.

Binance is gradually resuming crypto withdrawals following one of the largest security breaches in the crypto industry’s history, the latest among which are Zcash, TON, and Sui. Meanwhile, billions of dollars are flowing out of the exchange and Binance’s liquidity and user confidence are subject to close scrutiny.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

  • Binance Reopens Withdrawals Across 15 Crypto Networks
  • Stablecoins Return Across Major Chains
    • Binance Sees Billions Leave After $6.3B Hack
    • Withdrawal Recovery Becomes a Test of Binance Liquidity

Binance Reopens Withdrawals Across 15 Crypto Networks

Binance’s latest update added withdrawals for ZEC on Zcash, USDT and GRAM on TON, and SUI on Sui. Those are the networks that are linked to Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, XRP Ledger, Base, Dogecoin, Optimism, Arbitrum, Tron, Solana, Polygon and Avalanche C-Chain.

Latest Withdrawal Update

Withdrawals have now been re-enabled for the following networks and assets:

New:
✅ ZEC: ZEC
✅ TON: USDT, GRAM
✅ SUI: SUI

Already Enabled:
✅ BTC: BTC
✅ ETH: ETH, USDT, USDC
✅ BSC: BNB, USDT, USDC
✅ XRP: XRP
✅ Base: ETH, USDC
✅ DOGE: DOGE
✅ OP (Optimism): ETH, USDT, USDC
✅ ARBITRUM: ARB, ETH, USDT, USDC
✅ TRX: TRX, USDT
✅ SOL: SOL, USDT, USDC
✅ MATIC (Polygon): POL, USDT, USDC
✅ AVAXC: AVAX, USDT, USDC

We will continue to restore additional assets and networks in phases as security checks are completed. Further updates will be shared through official Binance channels.

— Binance (@binance) November 1, 2026

According to the exchange, it is attempting to restore the networks on a phased basis and every network is going through security and stability tests before withdrawals are turned on.

Read More: Binance $5.5B Hack Exposed: 50 EIP-7702 Nonces Opened One Hot Wallet in Minutes

Stablecoins Return Across Major Chains

Withdrawals of USDT and USDC are already enabled on several of Binance’s biggest supported networks, such as Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Polygon and Arbitrum.

This is particularly significant since they are a significant proportion of exchange liquidity and are frequently utilized by traders swapping assets between exchange spots. Binance has announced that more assets and networks will be returning once more checks are made.

Binance Sees Billions Leave After $6.3B Hack

Heavy withdrawal activity that orchestrated the reopening. DEFLI has recorded $5.8 billion in net outflows, while Binance has recorded roughly $3.64 billion in net outflows. Binance has an estimated $171 billion worth of customer assets, and the official net outflow was around 2.1% of the total customer assets, according to Reuters.

Withdrawals came after a massive security breach where approximately $6.3 billion in crypto assets were stolen.

The FBI blamed TraderTraitor hackers, linked to a North Korean insurgency, for the attack, said Reuters. Binance, in turn, has responded that it covered approximately $6 billion of the lost assets with its Secure Asset Fund for Users and futures insurance fund.

Withdrawal Recovery Becomes a Test of Binance Liquidity

One of the most definitive signs of user responses to the hack is the rate of withdrawals. People have requested withdrawals in large numbers after Binance resumed operations, but the withdrawals seem to have settled down in recent times, Binance stated. Meanwhile, gross withdrawals did not affect overall exchange reserves, as deposits kept coming in.

In the wake of the exchange, new hot wallet addresses have also had to be created as a security response and uploaded into the exchanges Proof of Reserves infrastructure.

The big one for traders will be what happens to the flow of funds as the rest of the networks are all back. In the meantime, Binance’s gradual reopening is a serious exercise in how effective its reserves, security measures, and customer faith will be if a massive attack is implemented.

title: Lumia – Why AI Agents Could Become the Biggest Owners of Real-World Assets
summary: Michael Huynh is Chief Marketing Officer at Lumia, a blockchain built specifically for tokenized real-world assets. It aims to handle an asset’s whole lifecycle, from compliant issuance to on-chain liquidity. Michael has worked full-time in crypto marketing since 2017, with Polygon, Avalanche and a ...
content:
Skip to content

Michael Huynh is Chief Marketing Officer at Lumia, a blockchain built specifically for tokenized real-world assets. It aims to handle an asset’s whole lifecycle, from compliant issuance to on-chain liquidity. Michael has worked full-time in crypto marketing since 2017, with Polygon, Avalanche and a few hundred other projects. He also co-founded the DCENTRAL conference series, which ran events across the US and into Asia.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Most of the RWA conversation so far has been about putting Treasuries on-chain and trading price exposure to gold. Michael argues that this barely scratches the surface; by his estimate, only about five percent of the opportunity has been unlocked. His real estate example shows what he means. Tokenizing a house is the easy part. The hard part is everything underneath it: deed settlement, county records, property taxes. Once those are bundled into the asset, mortgages and home equity lines of credit can follow it on-chain. The same reasoning turns tokenized gold from a trading instrument into a way for a mine to finance its next production run. That breadth is how Lumia positions itself against specialists like Ondo. Michael concedes they will win their chosen verticals, while Lumia tries to cover all the asset classes nobody has taken on yet.

The bigger bet is on the United States, and Michael is candid about what that costs. Lumia says it is deliberately building its US rails before the law arrives. He compares it to a racehorse that stays at the gate rather than wandering off to other tracks. The company has assembled a bipartisan bench of former Congressmen, including Tim Ryan and David McIntosh, with Gibson Dunn as counsel. The timing is pointed: the CLARITY Act failed a 49–50 cloture vote in the Senate in September. Michael says the stall was expected and that the US is still the market that matters, noting that institutions like BlackRock do not commit to a market without a path forward. He also explains LGP-01, which Lumia’s community passed with 95 percent support in early October. It retires the HyperNode program through a USDT buyback of future rewards and redirects the recovered tokens into a foundation fund for growth. He presents it as removing a structure that did not fit what institutional and government partners need.

The most provocative part of the conversation is about AI agents. Michael predicts, echoing Animoca Brands’ Yat Siu, that agents will become the largest holders of tokenized assets. He describes agents that score an asset against its listed price before buying, which speeds up price discovery. They would also source deals and send owners a daily summary, all within whatever permissions and spending limits the owner sets. A self-driving taxi that earns income around the clock is his example of an RWA category that does not exist on-chain yet. In the hot take round, Michael keeps at least half his heart with Bitcoin. He says agents combined with RWAs could take blockchain daily active users from one million to fifty million. He also sketches a ten-year future of reputation-based agent networks and “agentic billionaires”, and names The 100 as his favorite science fiction show.

title: Bitcoin Whitepaper Turns 18: How Satoshi’s 9-Page Vision Reshaped Global Finance
summary:
Key Takeaways: On October 31, 2008, the Bitcoin whitepaper was published by Satoshi Nakamoto, which outlines a peer-to-peer electronic cash system, without the need for banks. Eighteen years later, Bitcoin
The post Bitcoin Whitepaper Turns 18: How Satoshi’s 9-Page Vision Reshaped Global Finance appe...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • On October 31, 2008, the Bitcoin whitepaper was published by Satoshi Nakamoto, which outlines a peer-to-peer electronic cash system, without the need for banks.
  • Eighteen years later, Bitcoin developed from a novel monetary system to an asset owned by public organizations, investment funds, and governments.
  • Bitcoin Archive celebrated the occasion on its X page, restating the bold conclusion that the crypto industry began.

Bitcoin’s whitepaper was created on October 31st, 2008, marking 18 years in digital asset history. The initial allotment of nine pages of documents to send the funds without any process of money brokering has now become a worldwide network of trillions of dollars’ worth.

  • Satoshi Nakamoto Introduced a Different Way to Move Money
  • Bitcoin Has Moved Beyond Its Early Cypherpunk Community
    • The 18th Anniversary Brings Attention Back to Satoshi’s Idea

Satoshi Nakamoto Introduced a Different Way to Move Money

On October 31, 2008, an individual or group using the name Satoshi Nakamoto published Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System on a cryptography mailing list.

One major problem with online payments was that too often, financial institutions had to confirm the transfers of funds and avoid double spending. Satoshi envisioned a new peer-to-peer system that did not require central control to function: When people make an exchange, the transaction is verified using cryptographic proof, with a shared and publicly visible record containing the transactions.

This design was a distributed ledger plus proof-of-work. The miners confirm transactions, create new blocks, and miners are rewarded with transactions whenever the network follows the longest chain with largest proof-of-work.

On January 3, 2009, the Bitcoin network came into operation by mining the first block. This protocol later comes to be associated with a maximum supply of 21 million BTC and the assets are issued at a predictable time frame.

Read More: Michael Saylor Teases More Bitcoin After Strategy’s $69.45B Reserve Hits 848,250 BTC

Bitcoin Has Moved Beyond Its Early Cypherpunk Community

The network has since expanded well beyond the realm of cryptography, where the paper first appeared. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024, providing another channel for traditional investors to buy Bitcoin without owning cryptocurrency wallets.

Public companies are also including Bitcoin on their balance sheets. Some other examples include strategy being the largest publicly listed corporate holder and the U.S. government creating a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve in March 2025 using seized Bitcoins.

This represents a significant shift from Bitcoin’s early years, when every Bitcoin was dominated by technology enthusiasts and early adopters.

The 18th Anniversary Brings Attention Back to Satoshi’s Idea

Bitcoin Archive recently marked the occasion on X with a message celebrating 18 years of Bitcoin and thanking Satoshi Nakamoto. Another aspect of the network’s creation was also touched on in the post, the historic moment.

18 years of Bitcoin.

Thank you, Satoshi — what an incredible journey. https://t.co/DhYNB3SZ9y

— Bitcoin Archive (@BitcoinArchive) October 31, 2026

However, Bitcoin’s original concept has stayed true to its nature, allowing users to make transactions on a public network without a bank or payment company approving it.

Satoshi’s identity remains unknown, and the white paper’s publication began a project that would eventually influence thousands of other digital assets and blockchain networks.

title: Bank of England Opens Tokenized Collateral Door With 2027 Deadline for UK Clearing
summary:
Key Takeaways: The Bank of England is seeking input on tokenized collateral for central clearing. All tokenizable assets must be equally liquid and equally risky in terms of risk. The
The post Bank of England Opens Tokenized Collateral Door With 2027 Deadline for UK Clearing appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Bank of England is seeking input on tokenized collateral for central clearing.
  • All tokenizable assets must be equally liquid and equally risky in terms of risk.
  • The consultation will be open until Feb. 12, 2027.

The Bank of England comes closer and closer to introducing tokenized assets into the mainstream of the UK market infrastructure.

The central bank has launched a consultation outlining how central counterparties, or CCPs, could accept tokenized versions of eligible collateral without creating a separate regulatory regime for blockchain-based assets.

  • Bank of England Opens the Door to Tokenized Collateral
  • Same Risk, Same Regulatory Outcome
    • Stablecoins Could Enter the Conversation Later
    • UK Pushes Tokenization Deeper Into Wholesale Finance

Bank of England Opens the Door to Tokenized Collateral

The proposal concentrates on assets that are or could be already collaterized according to the UK’s CCP.

The Bank says tokenization by itself won’t bar an asset from being accepted. What’s important is whether the collateral remains easily transferable and saleable, has little credit risk and market risk, and can still be valued.

The Bank has reported that tokenization of collateral can facilitate trades of assets across markets and jurisdictions, particularly in meeting margin calls. Faster collateral movement could also reduce operational friction in clearing and support wider adoption of digital market infrastructure.

Read More: Blockchain.com and NYSE Target 24/7 Tokenized Stocks for 44 Million Crypto Accounts

Same Risk, Same Regulatory Outcome

The Bank is sticking to a simple rule: tokenized collateral should achieve the same regulatory result as traditional collateral. That means CCPs would need to show that digital representations of assets remain accessible and transferable even during stressed market conditions.

The regulator additionally urges firms to look at the risk associated with technology, custody arrangements and reliance on third-party infrastructure. For instance, tokenized security relying on a bridge that links blockchain records to other asset locations would require knowledge of the consequences of the bridge being compromised.

Stablecoins Could Enter the Conversation Later

The consultation doesn’t instantly add to the list of collaterals that are eligible. It primarily concentrates on the tokenisation of assets currently allowed under the existing regulations, such as cash, financial instruments, bank guarantees and gold, provided they meet established criteria.

But also the Bank´s position is seeking input from industry on a wider array of assets that may qualify in the future. That conversation also covers tokenized money market fund shares, tokenized gold, and stablecoins, so it’s applicable to the entire crypto ecosystem.

Some digital assets could eventually comply with existing collateral standards, the Bank said, and advised firms contemplating digital assets to reach out to supervisors early on.

UK Pushes Tokenization Deeper Into Wholesale Finance

The consultation is part of a wider consultation by the Bank of England, Financial Conduct Authority and HM Treasury in the UK. Their mission is to establish a more straightforward rule for tokenized securities and settlement in the digital medium, while fostering financial stability.

It will help foster responsible tokenization while maintaining the resilience of financial market infrastructure, said Deputy Governor for Financial Stability, Sarah Breeden. The consultation will continue through Feb. 12, 2027, and the Bank takes into account industry comments to decide its supervisory strategy.

title: Jupiter Lend Halts Withdrawals Amid $6.3B Binance Hack Fears Despite Zero Exposure
summary:
Key Takeaways: Following the liquidity crisis due to market turmoil after Binance’s security breach of $6.3 billion, Jupiter Lend has temporarily shut down withdrawals. The protocol claims it never had
The post Jupiter Lend Halts Withdrawals Amid $6.3B Binance Hack Fears Despite Zero Exposure appear...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Following the liquidity crisis due to market turmoil after Binance’s security breach of $6.3 billion, Jupiter Lend has temporarily shut down withdrawals.
  • The protocol claims it never had any exposure to Binance, there have been no funds on the exchange, no loss of funds to report.
  • Withdrawals are likely to begin once loans are repaid and new supplies are available.

Uncertainty about the security issue on Binance has been seeping into the crypto sector and dragging down Jupiter Lend. According to the Solana lending platform, its infrastructure is live, but users will have to wait for the withdrawal of liquidity.

Read More: Binance Says $6.3B Hit in Security Breach, $3B Frozen After DevOps Laptop Compromise

  • Jupiter Lend Faces Liquidity Crunch
  • Why Are Withdrawals Being Delayed?
    • USDC Withdrawable Balance Raises Concerns

Jupiter Lend Faces Liquidity Crunch

On October 30, Jupiter addressed withdrawal delays through its official X account, explaining that broader market conditions had created a liquidity shortage across its lending pools.

Due to broader market conditions, there is currently a liquidity crunch impacting withdrawals.

Market conditions will cause users to deposit or repay their loans. As they do so, withdrawals will be able to process again.

This is normal and expected during events like today’s. Liquidity will soon be available again.

The protocol is functioning as expected and all funds are safe.

— Jupiter Earn (@jupiter_earn) October 30, 2026

Withdrawals would be resumed as market players deposit their assets or repay their loans, the protocol said. It said the situation was normal at all times of significant market volatility and all funds belonging to users are safe.

The announcement came amid increasing security fears surrounding Binance and market actions by the broader crypto sector. Jupiter had earlier said that it was keeping an eye on development and had never had any direct exposure to Binance.

Users asked how there could be any contradiction between the earlier reassurance and the delays in withdrawal, to which Jupiter responded that both the things were correct.

It noted that Binance couldn’t raise any money and the protocol didn’t lose any. The withdrawal pressure is not directly related to the exchange incident, the team said and instead is an indicator of reactions from the wider market.

Read More: Binance $5.5B Hack Exposed: 50 EIP-7702 Nonces Opened One Hot Wallet in Minutes

Why Are Withdrawals Being Delayed?

Jupiter Lend gifts work by means of lending pools where a deposited good can be borrowed by items like Borrow and Multiply. This is because not all deposits will be available immediately as some assets may be used to make loans on the go.

Liquidity may not keep up with the demand for it in periods of heavy withdrawal demand. The repayment of borrowers and fresh money for deposits are therefore significant in restoring withdrawal capacity.

USDC Withdrawable Balance Raises Concerns

Jupiter’s API data aptly pointed to the magnitude of the liquidity situation. Around 418.5 million USDCs in Earn deposit claims, with accrued interest, were visible at 7.14 a.m. ET, whereas 3.35 USDCs were immediately available to withdraw.

This difference reflects the amount of the claims of depositors serviceable by the bank at a given time versus the liquid funds held by the bank. That is not, however, a finding of loan impairment nor a determination that depositors have been losing money on the underlying loans.

In addition to the above, Jupiter documents further withdrawals based on available amounts and permission to withdraw. Users might have to make smaller withdrawals or wait for returns of liquidity.

The withdrawal scenario comes amidst worries over Binance’s security breach, estimated to cause around $6.3 billion damage to Binance.

title: Tether Q3 Profit Hits $1.5B While USDT Reserve Buffer Nearly Doubles to $8B
summary:
Key Takeaways: In Q3, Tether achieved an operating profit of $1.5 billion. Reserve assets rose to almost $8 billion. U.S. Treasury exposure reached $132.4 billion. Tether also added another $1.5
The post Tether Q3 Profit Hits $1.5B While USDT Reserve Buffer Nearly Doubles to $8B appeared first on Cr...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • In Q3, Tether achieved an operating profit of $1.5 billion.
  • Reserve assets rose to almost $8 billion.
  • U.S. Treasury exposure reached $132.4 billion.

Tether also added another $1.5 billion in operating profits during the quarter, and considerably boosted the buffer for USDT. As of the end of September, the stablecoin issuer’s most recent BDO attestation reports $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities within total reserves.

Read More: Tether Backs Peso to Expand USDT Payments Across 4 Major Latin American Markets

  • Tether Reserve Buffer Jumps $3.8B in One Quarter
  • Treasury Holdings Drive Tether’s Earnings
    • Nine-Month Operating Profit Reaches $4.5B
    • USDT Still Controls More Than 60% of Stablecoins

Tether Reserve Buffer Jumps $3.8B in One Quarter

Tether’s surpluses surged from $4.1 billion at the end of June to $7.95 billion.

The increase added roughly $3.8 billion to the company’s reserve surplus in a single quarter. Total assets increased to $191.45 billion with total liabilities reaching $183.50 billion, with a majority of the liabilities held by digital tokens issued being about $183.47 billion.

USDT issuance demonstrated overall strength at approximately $184 billion despite fluctuations in market sentiment for cryptocurrencies during the first nine months of 2026.

Treasury Holdings Drive Tether’s Earnings

Tether said U.S. Treasury bills and reverse re-purchase agreements continued to be the primary sources of operating income. As of September 30 government debt represented the primary asset of the reserve portfolio exceeding $132.4 billion via direct and indirect holdings of Treasury bills.

That asset allocation will give them significant short-term liquidity, in short-term, liquid bonds, that can support redeeming when the market is in a state of stress.

Nine-Month Operating Profit Reaches $4.5B

Tether generated $4.5 billion in net operating profit during the first three quarters of 2026.

Q3’s operating profit was reported at $1.5 billion, on par with in Q2. Tether said it had $4.11 billion in reserve for the second quarter, and that number grew dramatically for Q3.

The higher surplus provides Tether with more liquidity to redeem tokens and cover the cost of maintaining infrastructure during tough market conditions, CEO Paolo Ardoino wrote.

The statistics were revealed after Tether underwent its first full independent financial statement audit in August. KPMG U.S. gave an unqualified opinion for the company’s 2025 financial statements.

Read More: Tether Clears First-Ever KPMG Audit, Revealing a $6.8B Cushion for Crypto Markets

USDT Still Controls More Than 60% of Stablecoins

Despite the USDT circulating market capitalization dropping below the $184 billion USDT issuance figure reported in the quarter-end statement, USDT remains the largest dollar-backed token.

DefiLlama revealed that USDT netted a market capitalization of approximately USD 180 billion on 30 October, with the overall market of stablecoins valued at nearly USD 297 billion. This means the USDT is around 60.6% dominant.

The gap indicates the difference between Tether’s September 30 reporting date and the current market data at a point in time circulating.

As excess reserves near $8 billion and the portfolio is heavily weighted with Bitcoin securities, Tether will go into 2026’s 4th quarter with a considerably healthier financial cushion to support the crypto market’s most prominent stable coin.
